title: Letitia James stumped by debate question while GOP rival delivers 'zinger for the ages'
summary: Letitia James went silent for several seconds when asked to name a former AG she admired during the Thursday New York Attorney General debate.
story: New York AG Letitia James struggled to name a former attorney general she admired during Thursday’s debate, prompting a sharp response from Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy. (Credit: Spectrum News NY1, Oct. 8)

New York Democratic Attorney General Letitia James went silent for several seconds when asked to name a former state attorney general she admired during Thursday's New York attorney general race debate.
"Tick tock," Errol Louis of Spectrum News 1, one of the moderators said to James, prompting laughter from the Attorney General.

The attorney general's race in New York comes against the backdrop of James' ongoing dispute with President Donald Trump, who called James "a Complete and Total Disaster" and accused her of leading a "WITCH Hunt" against him in his endorsement of James' Republican challenger, Saritha Komatireddy, in August.
LETITIA JAMES' UNDERDOG RIVAL TURNS AG'S OWN PLAYBOOK AGAINST HER WITH SCATHING 52-COUNT CAMPAIGN 'INDICTMENT'
New York Attorney General Letitia James speaks during an announcement on the Standing Up to ICE outreach program at the governor's office in New York City, Aug. 12, 2026. (REUTERS/David Dee Delgado)

The pause from James drew immediate criticism from Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor and chief of staff for the Drug Enforcement Administration, who quipped from the podium that James "only admires herself."
"An absolutely devastating moment for Tish James," conservative communications strategist Steve Guest wrote on X. "'She only admires herself' is a debate zinger for the ages."
"No, no, no, no, we admire others," James said. "I admire all of the past attorney generals because it is a difficult job and you've got to stand up."
When asked the same question, Komatireddy named Dennis Vacco, who served as the state's attorney general from 1995 to 1998. Like Komatireddy, he was also a former federal prosecutor.
James then said that she admired former Democratic Attorney General Bob Abrams, who served from 1979 to 1993.
The exchange, which came in the final moments of Thursday's debate, led critics to question whether James knew of other New York attorneys general.

"Very telling moment," Steve McLaughlin, Rensselaer County executive, wrote on X. "James went completely blank because she's A: dumb as a rock B: has no idea who any former AG is because she's not doing the job and never has been."
NY AG HOPEFUL BLASTS LETITIA JAMES AS MEDICAID FRAUD RECOVERIES COLLAPSE: 'SHE'S NOT DOING THE JOB'

Republican candidate for New York Attorney General Saritha Komatireddy holds a news conference with state GOP lawmakers on increasing public transit safety in New York on Wednesday, April 29, 2026, at West Capitol Park in Albany, N.Y. (Will Waldron/Albany Times Union via Getty Images))
"She's a mouthpiece," McLaughlin continued. "Zero institutional knowledge."
"Letitia James doesn't know the plural form of 'Attorney General,'" another Twitter user wrote.
Nicole Kiprilov, a spokesperson for Komatireddy, echoed the candidate's comment on the debate stage.

"Letitia James can’t name a single former Attorney General she admires because she’s too busy admiring herself. She’s turned the Attorney General’s office into her own political stage and ignored the safety of the state," Kiprilov said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "New Yorkers deserve a real prosecutor, not a joke like her!"
But James' campaign pushed back on Komatireddy's characterization of James and how she runs her office.

"Attorney General Letitia James spent much of the debate teaching her opponent how the Office of the Attorney General actually works, and she was happy to name former Attorney General Bob Abrams as someone she respects,"  a spokesperson for James said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

General view of the now-shuttered Chi Phi fraternity house at 107 Edgemoor Lane in Ithaca, NY., Tueaday, October 6, 2026.  (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

Kathy Hochul appointed James as special investigator to examine an alleged gang rape that occurred at Cornell University in October 2024. The renewed attention comes in response to a recent lawsuit filed by the alleged victim, Jane Doe, against the university, the alleged perpetrators, her sorority and a bar that allegedly served her alcohol while she was underage.

But James has faced calls from an attorney for one of the defendants to recuse herself from the case over social media posts showing support for Jane Doe before James was appointed special investigator.

title: Kash Patel announces arrest of suspected ShinyHunters co-conspirator after FBI jobs portal breach
summary: FBI Director Kash Patel says agents arrested a suspected ShinyHunters co-conspirator tied to the FBIjobs.gov data breach and third-party vendor hack.
story: Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory special agent turned CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies, explains how stolen personal and assignment information could be exploited while stressing there is no evidence hackers accessed classified FBI systems.

FBI Director Kash Patel announced Friday that agents arrested another suspected co-conspirator linked to the ShinyHunters hacking group earlier this week during the bureau's investigation of a cybersecurity incident involving its jobs website.
The arrest is the latest in a series of FBI actions against the hacking network in recent days, according to Patel, who said investigators are pursuing additional leads and evidence.

"Earlier this week, our agents in the field arrested another suspected co-conspirator of the ShinyHunters group, the group believed to be responsible for the recent FBIjobs.gov incident, which occurred on a platform managed by a third-party vendor," Patel said in an Oct. 9 statement.
FBI INVESTIGATES AFTER SHINYHUNTERS HACKERS CLAIM THEFT OF AGENTS' PERSONAL DATA
FBI Director Kash Patel speaks during a news conference Oct. 23, 2025, in New York City. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Patel said the FBI is working with its partners to dismantle the group and its associates.

"This arrest demonstrates the strength and reach of our efforts to protect Americans from cybercrime. We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what’s left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate."

ShinyHunters, a criminal hacking and extortion group, previously said it obtained sensitive personal information belonging to FBI employees and applicants through the bureau's jobs portal.16-YEAR-OLD ALLEGEDLY LED RANSOMWARE GANG BEHIND HUNDREDS OF ATTACKS

The group said it stole information belonging to nearly all FBI agents and people who applied to work for the bureau, Reuters previously reported. A sample of data shared with the outlet contained agents' names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, assignments and, in some cases, names of family members.

The FBI previously said it was investigating whether the breach originated within its own systems or through a third-party provider supporting FBIJobs.gov. The extent of the alleged breach has not been independently confirmed.

Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory special agent and CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies, previously told Fox News Digital the distinction between stolen personnel information and access to classified investigative systems is critical.
FBI HACK CLAIM RAISES FEARS OVER SENSITIVE PERSONAL DATA
FBI investigators monitor digital threats as questions remain over how the FBIJobs.gov incident occurred and what information may have been exposed. (FBI)

"There is a meaningful difference between somebody obtaining personnel information and somebody gaining access to classified investigative systems," Pack said. "Based on what we know right now, there is no indication they have the keys to the kingdom."

A representative for the Department of Justice did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Trump names Leavitt successor after weeks of speculation — and she's no stranger to MAGA
summary: Katie Zacharia has been offered a job as the next White House Press Secretary
story: On her final day as press secretary, Karoline Leavitt reveals on 'Fox & Friends' that she's privately advised President Trump on her White House replacement.

President Donald Trump tapped a trusted ally from the company behind his Truth Social platform to become his next White House press secretary Friday, naming attorney and television commentator Katie Zacharia to succeed Karoline Leavitt.
Two White House officials confirmed the selection to Fox News Digital before Trump publicly announced the appointment on X.

Zacharia, an attorney and frequent television commentator, currently serves as senior communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the president's social media platform, Truth Social. She will succeed former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt.

"It is my Great Honor to have just appointed, as Press Secretary, Katie Zacharia. Katie currently serves as Senior Communications Advisor to Truth Social (Trump Media & Technology Group), where she has been outstanding!" Trump wrote Friday afternoon.
KAROLINE LEAVITT JOINS FOX NEWS AS CONTRIBUTOR AFTER LEAVING WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE
Katie Zacharia was named the new White House press secretary. (Barry Morgenstein )
Zacharia celebrated the appointment in a post on X, thanking Trump for what she called the "distinguished privilege" of serving as White House press secretary.

"Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime," Zacharia wrote. "President Trump has shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day. His confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country."
Zacharia said her focus would be on communicating the administration's accomplishments to the American public while working with reporters across the country.

"The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day," she wrote. "I look forward to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out."
She also acknowledged the expectations that come with succeeding Leavitt.
"Following the fabulous Karoline Leavitt is a high standard, and one worth meeting," Zacharia wrote.

Zacharia previously served briefly as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security following the departure of Tricia McLaughlin, who had served as press secretary under former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem.
KAROLINE LEAVITT HEADS FOR WHITE HOUSE EXIT AS SPECULATION BUILDS OVER WHO TRUMP PICKS NEXT

Katie Zacharia and Adam Weiss attend as Jean Shafiroff Hosts Holiday Party in Honor of New York Women's Foundation at Private Residence on December 16, 2024 in New York City. (Patrick McMullan via Getty Images))

"Katie is a distinguished Graduate of Pepperdine University, and the Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, an attorney, and a frequent Commentator on outlets, including Fox News and Newsmax. She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7. She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," said Trump.

"She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA! I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration. Katie is replacing the fabulous Karoline Leavitt, who did a fantastic job as Press Secretary. Good luck Katie," he added.

A 41-year-old mother of four, Zacharia has been married to her husband Tyler since 2011. He is a producer known for projects like the 2019 film "The Irishman" and 2025 movie, "Roofman." Zacharia notes on her Instagram that her husband has also worked with Angel Studios on "David," "Brink of War" and "Young Washington."
WHITE HOUSE PLANS GUEST HOSTS FOR PRESS BRIEFINGS WHILE KAROLINE LEAVITT TAKES MATERNITY LEAVE
Caitlin Sinclair , Adam Weiss and Katie Zacharia seen on election night 2024. (Adam Weiss)
Since Leavitt's departure, there have been only two formal White House press briefings — one with Vice President JD Vance and one with Attorney General Todd Blanche.
The White House adopted a rotating lineup of top Trump administration officials to lead press briefings while former press secretary Karoline Leavitt was on maternity leave over the summer.

"Katie has been an effective champion of MAGA movement and America First policies - and most importantly clearly has [the] trust of President Trump," former Trump press secretary Sean Spicer told Fox News Digital.

"Anyone who has not met her yet will quickly see that she is a genuinely kind person who will work well with the press corps, unlike the first press secretary who came across as an angry leprechaun at times," Spicer added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Secretary of State Marco Rubio kicked off the rotation, followed by Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. Rather than relying on a single deputy press secretary, the administration tapped high-profile officials to field questions from reporters on the president’s agenda.

Names previously floated as potential replacements for Leavitt included former Trump attorney and current Justice Department adviser Alina Habba, CNN political commentator Scott Jennings, principal deputy White House press secretary Anna Kelly, White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, former Pence communications director Katie Miller, White House communications director Steven Cheung and Breitbart Washington bureau chief Matthew Boyle.
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Marco Rubio announces sweeping financial sanctions against the International Criminal Court
summary: Marco Rubio announced the Trump administration will soon freeze ICC assets and bar all U.S. transactions with the International Criminal Court.
story: Secretary of State Marco announced Friday that the Trump administration is sanctioning the International Criminal Court, arguing it does not have the power to prosecute American citizens and leaders.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Friday that the Trump administration is imposing sweeping financial sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), a body the president has sought to dismantle throughout his second term.
To date, the administration has sanctioned 17 individuals with ties to the ICC, including judges and prosecutors. The latest move marks the first time the U.S. has gone after the institution itself.

"Our message is clear: The United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC," Rubio said in a pre-recorded video message released Friday morning. "Both parties agree on this, but only President Trump has the resolve to take the action needed to end this threat once and for all."
This comes hours after this year's Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a former ICC judge.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Portuguese Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel (not seen) give a joint news conference at the Necessidades Palace, the Portuguese foreign ministry, in Lisbon Oct. 8, 2026. (Zed Jameson/Anadolu via Getty Images)
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SANCTIONS SITTING PRESIDENT OF THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT FOR 'ABUSES OF POWER'
In a statement Friday, the Netherlands-based court strongly condemned the U.S. sanctions as "an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order."

"This measure targets an independent judicial institution, created by treaty and entrusted by 125 States Parties with investigating and prosecuting genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression," the ICC added.
"It is an attempt to obstruct the course of justice and to prevent the Court from doing what it was created to do."
ICC President Tomoko Akane, who was personally sanctioned by the Trump administration in August, said the court will continue to operate despite the new penalties.

In announcing the sanctions, Rubio argued the ICC believes it has the authority to prosecute American service members operating overseas and even U.S. Border Patrol agents. There is no evidence the court has sought to investigate or prosecute Border Patrol agents, though Rubio previously raised that possibility in July.

International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane speaks to to reporters after meeting with members of the European Parliament's Human Rights Committee in Brussels, Belgium, March 19, 2025. (Dursun Aydemir/Anadolu via Getty Images)
WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

The administration's concerns about U.S. personnel are not entirely hypothetical. In 2017, an ICC prosecutor sought authorization to investigate alleged war crimes committed by U.S. military and intelligence personnel in Afghanistan.

ICC judges initially rejected the request, but that decision was overturned on appeal in 2020, allowing the investigation to proceed. The court's prosecutor later de-prioritized alleged crimes involving U.S. personnel to focus on alleged crimes committed by the Taliban and ISIS-K.
Under the new sanctions, any ICC assets subject to U.S. jurisdiction will be frozen, while Americans, U.S. businesses and banks are generally barred from conducting transactions with the court.
The sanctions will not go into effect immediately. The Treasury Department has given the ICC a 180-day general license to maintain its operations, giving the court time to address U.S. concerns.
An exterior view of the International Criminal Court Oct. 9, 2026, in The Hague, Netherlands. (Pierre Crom/Getty Images)
ICC TURNS 'BLIND EYE' TO TOP WORLD THREATS WHILE TARGETING AMERICANS, TRUMP ADMIN SAYS

"Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. And we expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American service members for their defense, to rein in this rogue court," Rubio said.
"If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC piece by piece until Americans are threatened no longer."

One of the other major grievances the administration has with the ICC is its decision to issue arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant in 2024.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks during the state memorial ceremony for the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attacks, at Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem Oct. 5, 2026. (Debbie Hill/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The ICC argued both officials were responsible for war crimes and crimes against humanity against Palestinians in Gaza during Israel's military response to the Hamas-led Oct. 7 terrorist attacks in 2023. Both men have denied wrongdoing.

In a February 2025 executive order authorizing sanctions against ICC officials, President Donald Trump called the arrest warrants "baseless" and said the court overstepped its authority since Israel was not an ICC member.

The ICC maintains that it can exercise jurisdiction over nationals of non-member states when they are accused of qualifying crimes committed on the territory of a state that has accepted the court’s jurisdiction.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Dem scrambles to change tune on trans athletes as Trump targets past record: ‘Annie Trannie’
summary: South Carolina U.S. Senate candidate Annie Andrews claims she was misrepresented on transgender sports after Trump dubbed her "Annie Trannie."
story: Dr. Annie Andrews, the Democratic Senate nominee in solidly red South Carolina, tells Fox News Digital she rejects biological men in women's sports, gender surgeries for minors

A South Carolina Democrat running for U.S. Senate who previously opposed legislation restricting transgender athletes' participation in girls' sports is now emphasizing her opposition to biological males participating in female athletics as President Donald Trump targets her record ahead of the midterm elections.

Trump took aim at Annie Andrews, a pediatrician challenging Republican Sen. Darline Graham, in a series of Truth Social posts this week, dubbing her "Annie Trannie" and accusing her of supporting transgender policies that are out of step with South Carolina voters.

The president also shared an attack ad accusing Andrews of supporting biological males competing against female athletes. "Annie Andrews is for they/them, not for our values, not for South Carolina," the ad said.
But Andrews pushed back in an interview with Fox News Digital on Thursday, arguing that her positions have been misrepresented.
"I don't support biological men playing in women's sports and I don't support gender surgery on minors," Andrews said.

Her comments stand in contrast to her public opposition to South Carolina's 2022 Save Women’s Sports Act, which restricted transgender athletes' participation in girls' and women's school sports. At the time, Andrews called the legislation "shameful" and "actively harmful," raising questions about how she reconciles her past opposition to the law with her current campaign position.
DEMOCRATS ARE CHANGING THEIR TRANSGENDER MESSAGE. REPUBLICANS SAY THEY’RE JUST FLIP-FLOPPING
Annie Andrews, candidate for U.S. Senate, speaks with people Monday, March 30, 2026, during the campaign event in Greenville, South Carolina. (REUTERS)

As passed, the bill required interscholastic, intercollegiate, intramural and club teams sponsored by public schools and colleges to be designated as male or female-coded. It then closed women’s teams to male students and similarly closed men’s sports to women — unless the school did not have a designated women’s team. Private schools competing against public schools were required to follow the same rules.
It also allowed students harmed by a violation to sue schools.
Andrews’ social media post at the time garnered resurfaced attention as she launched her 2026 Senate bid, attracting pressure from Republicans.
"Annie "Trannie" Andrews is running against our wonderful Darline Graham for the Senate in South Carolina," Trump wrote in one post.

"Annie Trannie is not, in particular, as it pertains to representing the Values of the Great People of South Carolina — She is in favor of Transgender for Everyone, Open Borders, Defunding the Police, High Taxes, a Weak Military, and will absolutely fight to take your guns away — In other words, she is against our Great Second Amendment! Trannie is not for South Carolina, and South Carolina must show, in the upcoming Election, that it is not for her," Trump added.
In her interview with Fox News Digital, Andrews dismissed Trump's barb, calling it a distraction from the issues central to voters in South Carolina.

"And in regards to the name-calling, if calling me names is going to lower gas and diesel prices here for so many hardworking South Carolinian families, if it’s going to lower grocery prices or somehow make healthcare more affordable then he can call me all the names he wants but I don’t think that’s a path to solution so I’m going to stay focused on what I can do to help folks in South Carolina," Andrews said.

Andrews did not immediately respond to additional requests for comment on whether her statements reflected a change in stance. She also did not expand on what had drawn criticism for the Save Women’s Sports Act.
TALARICO CAMP SAYS HE OPPOSES TRANS ATHLETES IF UNSAFE OR UNFAIR BUT ACCUSES POLITICIANS OF BULLYING STUDENTS
President Donald Trump attends a campaign rally at the Freeman Coliseum in San Antonio, Texas, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. (Alex Brandon/AP)
At least one Republican onlooker, National Republican Senatorial Regional Press Secretary Nick Puglia, believes her remarks speaks poorly of the message she's presenting to voters.

"Annie Andrews' blatant lies show just how desperate she is and how little she thinks of South Carolinians. But nothing Andrews says or does will change her far-left record," Puglia said in a comment.

This isn't the first time Andrews has received Republican criticisms for what they view as retreats from trans policies. In 2022, Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., called out Andrews for, in her view, trying to walk back her opposition to H. 4047, a bill that would "prohibit the performance of a medical procedure or the prescription or issuance of medication, upon or to a minor, that is intended to alter the appearance of the minor's gender or delay puberty, with exceptions; to create criminal penalties; and for other purposes."
Andrews said she opposed the bill in a post to X, calling it "dangerous," only to later say that she opposed trans procedures for minors.

"She called thewww.youtube.comwww.youtube.com legislation to ban that kind of surgery dangerous. She called that legislation an attack on our youth. And it wasn't until we called her out on it that she decided that she's now not for something that she was very publicly in support of just last year. And so it's really hard to play hide and seek from your public comments, because once you tweet it, it's on their public record forever. And that's how we discovered it," Mace told Fox News Digital at the time.

Notably, she isn’t the only Democrat who in recent weeks has received attention for seeming shifts in her position over transgender policies. Fellow Democrats like Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, Rep. Don Davis, D-N.C., and Sarah Trone Garriott, a congressional candidate in Iowa, have all been forced to reiterate their positions as Republicans have highlighted their records on the subject.
WATCH: BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT CALLED IOWA A 'BACKWATER' OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES BAN

Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, attends a news conference being conducted by Speaker of the House Mike Johnson in the Rayburn Room at the U.S. Capitol on Oct. 29, 2025 in Washington, D.C.  (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

In Kaptur’s case, she described how she had "voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of our schools" despite voting against a women’s sports bill. Similarly, Davis voted "present" on that same women’s bill while later claiming that women should have "safe and fair space" in sports. And Garriott, who cast a vote against a ban on biological men in women’s locker rooms, clarified her stance earlier this year, stating that "I oppose letting men in women’s locker rooms."
Those statements reflect broader trends in public opinion showing consensus on trans athlete policies.

Recently, the Pew Research Center found in a Aug. 11 report that 73% of respondents were "not at all" or "not too" comfortable with "athletes competing on sports teams that do not match their sex at birth," compared to just 13% that replied that they were "extremely" or "very" comfortable with the idea. Similarly, 66% of participants said they would support laws or policies requiring trans athletes to compete on teams that match their biological sex compared to 15% who said they would oppose such policies.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

With just four weeks left to address criticisms over her views, Andrews now heads to South Carolina’s general election on Nov. 3., having cleared the state's Democratic primary earlier this year in June.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: Trump sets up committee to investigate Fed Governor Lisa Cook over mortgage fraud allegations
summary: President Donald Trump's new White House committee will hear mortgage fraud allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in a closed hearing.
story: Chief legal correspondent Shannon Bream details the Supreme Court's latest rulings, including a decision in Trump v. Slaughter affirming the president's power to dismiss a Federal Trade Commission commissioner. However, in Trump v. Cook, the court states the president cannot unilaterally fire a Federal Reserve governor. These opinions shape executive power and independent agencies.

President Donald Trump has set up a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over allegations she made false statements on mortgage documents, the same accusations Trump has cited for over a year in a bid to remove her from office.

Trump attempted to remove Cook in August 2025, triggering a lengthy legal battle that culminated in the Supreme Court blocking her firing in June 2026. In a 5-4 ruling, the court ruled she had not been given adequate time to respond to the allegations against her.

This newly-formed committee appears to be the process the White House has settled on to give Cook a chance to advocate for herself, as she will be allowed to submit a written statement ahead of her first scheduled hearing on Nov. 5, 2026.
Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook participates in a board meeting at the Federal Reserve on March 19, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
WHO IS LISA COOK? THE CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR AT THE HEART OF THE SUPREME COURT’S TRUMP-FED SHOWDOWN

Her statement must be received by the committee at least three days ahead of the hearing, which will unfold at the White House and will last no more than four hours, according to a notice dated Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026, but released on Friday by the Trump administration.

At the hearing itself, Cook will be able to "present argument, written evidence, and written witness statements regarding the evidence and allegations," the White House said. In turn, lawyers with the Department of Justice will question her.
The hearing will be closed to the public but will be transcribed.
U.S. President Donald Trump gestures after speaking to the media as he departs the White House on Oct. 1, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)
EXPLAINED: HOW LISA COOK’S THREE HOME LOANS BECAME CENTRAL TO TRUMP’S FIGHT OVER HER FEDERAL RESERVE SEAT

Three White House staffers, including National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett, will serve as members of the committee. Hassett was one of Trump's top picks to replace Jerome Powell as Fed Chair before he ultimately settled on Kevin Warsh.

The White House said it expects Cook to submit another written statement after the hearing, after which the committee will make a recommendation to Trump on whether there is adequate cause to remove her from her post.
The White House revisited its effort to fire Cook in August, sending her a letter informing her that Trump was once again considering terminating her.

National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett speaks to reporters outside the West Wing after a video interview on the North Lawn of the White House on Sept. 4, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
This time, Cook was given 21 days to respond. Her attorneys submitted a letter to the White House on Aug. 26 denying that she had committed mortgage fraud.
The White House alleged that Cook claimed homes in Atlanta and Michigan as her primary residence on separate mortgage agreements and later rented out the Atlanta property.

Cook's attorney said the Atlanta designation was an inadvertent mistake, arguing that she sought financing for it as a vacation home and consistently identified Michigan as her "primary" or "permanent" residence.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Denver, Boulder ignored ICE detainers for migrants with child abuse, assault arrests, House GOP report reveals
summary: Jim Jordan's committee names illegal immigrants accused of violent crimes whose ICE detainers were allegedly ignored in both Denver and Boulder.
story: Former NYPD Lt. Darrin Porcher discusses sanctuary city policies following the arrest of two illegal immigrants accused of stabbing and robbing an off-duty detective in the Bronx.
FIRST ON FOX: A blue state's law enforcement officials are keeping illegal immigrants accused of violent crimes out of the reach of federal authorities, a new report claims.
The House Judiciary Committee, led by Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, released new findings Friday in its investigation into sanctuary jurisdictions and their impact on law enforcement across the country.

The latest is a 25-page report that accuses top prosecutors in Denver and Boulder of helping illegal immigrants evade Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), while also revealing for the first time the names and graphic charges against some of those whom House GOP investigators say are being shielded from President Donald Trump's federal crackdown.
Both the district attorneys for Denver and Boulder pushed back against Republicans' accusations.
JIM JORDAN SUBPOENAS BLUE STATE DAS ACCUSED OF 'PREFERENTIAL TREATMENT' FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CRIMINALS
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents walk a detainee out of the Ventura County Government Center in Ventura, Calif., on July 27, 2026. (Blake Fagan/AFP via Getty Images)
Among the list is "Fernando Barrios-Ramirez, a Venezuelan national arrested for sexual assault on a child," the report said.

Denver District Attorney John Walsh told Fox News Digital, "Unfortunately, in Barrios-Ramirez’s case, we were prevented from pursuing a decades-long sentence by ICE,  who deported Barrios-Ramirez to Mexico over our objection, effectively setting him free."
Walsh said his office prosecuted other cases listed in the report as well.

Another alleged criminal Denver is accused of ignoring an ICE detainer for is Juan Andres Holguin-Mendez, a Mexican national whose "criminal history also includes arrests for willful cruelty to a child, DUI, malicious mischief, possession of a controlled substance, trespassing, disturbing the peace, and evading a peace officer."
Holguin-Mendez was arrested for damage to property, the report said.
A Venezuelan national named Diego Cano-Diaz with multiple alleged protective order violations was "arrested for aggravated assault with a weapon, resisting arrest, and assault," the report said.
At least four illegal immigrants were arrested due to alleged domestic violence in Denver but also had their ICE detainers ignored, the report said.
WATCH: DEM DEMANDS 'ONE CASE' WHERE SANCTUARY CITIES DIDN'T TURN OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS; DHS PROVIDES LIST
The House Judiciary Committee said Boulder County prosecutors weigh immigration status when deciding how to proceed with an alleged crime. (House Judiciary Committee)
In Boulder, "Mario Hernandez-Quiroz, a Mexican national arrested for child abuse and failure to appear," was among those whose ICE detainer was ignored.

Ignoring an ICE detainer does not necessarily mean law enforcement released the accused back onto public streets. It does, however, delay potential federal deportation proceedings to ensure the accused does not stay in the U.S.
DHS BOSS REVEALS OVAL OFFICE PLAN TO 'WITHHOLD FUNDING' FROM SANCTUARY CITIES AFTER AGGRESSIVE NEW YORK BUST

But the report did accuse district attorneys in Denver and Boulder of helping illegal immigrants suspected of criminal acts to evade ICE, including being more lenient with their treatment in order to avoid federal immigration proceedings — in effect, accusing them of letting more undocumented criminals back onto the streets.

The report said suspected Tren de Aragua gang member Abraham Smith Gonzalez was released after ICE only got up to two hours' notice, allegedly resulting in an officer's assault when federal authorities sought to arrest him. (House Judiciary Committee)

For instance, House GOP investigators said they obtained internal documents that show the Denver Sheriff's Department provided written explanations in a suspected illegal immigrant criminal's preferred language that said they have "the right to refuse to speak to federal immigration authorities."
DENVER MAN’S ESCAPE EXPOSES CHILLING TREN DE ARAGUA KIDNAPPING PLOT THAT LANDS TRIO IN PRISON
The report also accused Denver officials of providing insufficient notice when they do notify ICE about suspected illegal immigrant criminals.
An example highlighted in the report involved a suspected Tren de Aragua gang member, about whom ICE was given "between one and two hours' notice to take him into custody."

The suspected gang member, Abraham Smith Gonzalez, was subsequently released, the report said, and "as a result, when ICE officers attempted to arrest Gonzalez outside a Denver jail in 2025, he assaulted one officer."
The House Judiciary Committee said Boulder County prosecutors weigh immigration status when deciding how to proceed with an alleged crime. (House Judiciary Committee)
The report also accused both Boulder and Denver prosecutors of weighing immigration consequences when pursuing charges against an individual.
DOJ ACCUSES MARYLAND OF 'ACTIVE AND DELIBERATE EFFORT' TO PREVENT DEPORTATIONS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS: LAWSUIT

"In Boulder, District Attorney Dougherty prohibits information sharing with ICE," the report said. "Before President Trump even took office in January 2025, Dougherty emailed Boulder defense attorneys to remind them of his office’s pro-illegal alien policies, including his office’s consideration of collateral immigration consequences."

An excerpt that the report noted is part of Boulder County District Attorney's Office guidance stating that attorneys "consider the immigration and other collateral consequences to a defendant in recommending dispositions."
House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, speaks at a press conference with other members of House Republican leadership in Washington, D.C., on May 20, 2025. (Getty Images)
Both Denver and Boulder encourage suspected illegal immigrants to not cooperate with ICE unless a judicial warrant is presented, the report said.
ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF SEXUALLY ASSAULTING CHILDREN AFTER FAIRFAX COUNTY RELEASE: DHS
Dougherty in Boulder has already been targeted by Jordan's probe, with the Ohio Republican subpoenaing Dougherty and accusing him of failing to sufficiently cooperate.

He told Fox News Digital in response to the report, "This report is a political stunt to sway voters before the midterm elections. My responsibility is to do justice, enhance public safety, and fight for victims. I’m not going to be distracted by political theatre or intimidated into abandoning my responsibility to protect the community and uphold the law. I am proud of our amazing and dedicated staff. They work incredibly hard to uphold the best interests of Boulder County and Colorado. It is my privilege to work alongside the outstanding women and men in the District Attorney’s Office."
Dougherty's office also accused committee Republicans of "intentionally" misrepresenting one individual's case in its report that was not mentioned in this article.

"Under the Republicans’ approach, Contreras would have been released to ICE and immediately deported. That would have been a violation of state law. Also, Contreras would be free in another country with no consequences for his criminal conduct, the harm to the victim, and the risk he poses to the community," the office said. "Under Boulder County’s approach, the Sheriff complied with state law and, ultimately, Contreras was held fully accountable by the prosecutors in our office and sent to state prison for eight (8) years. When he completes that sentence, he will then face deportation."

Walsh told Fox News Digital, "The men and women of the Denver District Attorney’s Office work tirelessly every day and every night to protect community safety and have helped achieve historic reductions in crime in Denver.  Our immigration collateral consequences policy closely tracks the guidance of the United States Supreme Court in Padilla v. Kentucky, and not only complies with the law, but advances community safety by ensuring that convictions are not subsequently overturned."

"The Denver Sheriff’s Department is responsible for addressing ICE detainers and does so in full compliance with Colorado law and the requirements of the United States Constitution," Walsh said.

title: Radical anti-Trump language riddles California voter guide on high-stakes ballot measure
summary: California's Prop 39 voter ID ballot guide draws backlash online for its politically charged language, including a reference to "MAGA billionaires."
story: Fox News senior national correspondent William La Jeunesse reports on a judge siding with California’s attorney general in a voter ID ballot fight on ‘America Reports.’
A California ballot measure on voter identification provides voters with guidance replete with far-left jargon, including a dig at "MAGA billionaires," that has turned heads online.

Proposition 39 is a citizen-led effort, organized by a group called Californians for Voter ID, that submitted 1.3 million signatures in favor of the ballot initiative in March — far outpacing the required nearly 875,000 signatures in order for it to be adopted as a ballot measure.

Californians are slated to vote on the voter ID initiative in November. If approved, it would require a government-issued identification card or number to vote in person or by mail. It would also require election officials to verify U.S. citizenship.
But the language explaining the proposition from those who oppose the measure in the California voters guide has been flagged online for its highly political nature.

A volunteer picks up "Require Voter ID" sign at the press conference at the Riverside County Registrar of Voters on Monday, March 2, 2026, as GOP lawmakers gather in support of placing a voter ID measure on the November ballot.  (Anjali Sharif-Paul/MediaNews Group/The Sun via Getty Images)
SEN MARK WARNER CALLED OUT IN ABC INTERVIEW FOR INACCURATE VOTER ID CLAIMS
Groups that support the initiative are allowed to argue in favor of it on the ballot, while groups opposed are allowed to do the same on the ballot.

"No on Prop. 39," begins the arguments section on the ballot initiative. "This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars."
"Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No," it concludes.
Opponents of the measure are listed as the ACLU California Action, Common Cause and the League of Women Voters of California.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom and President Donald Trump. The Trump administration this week announced a pause on more than $10 billion in childcare funds to five blue states. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images (left); Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images (right))
INSIDE HOUSE REPUBLICANS' PLAN TO END RUN DEM OPPOSITION AND PASS TRUMP-BACKED VOTER ID
The summary section of the ballot measure in the guide states the expected financial impact should the measure take effect.
"Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements," it says.
A third section titled "What Your Vote Means" also features language describing the ramifications of voting "yes" or "no" on the initiative.

"A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote," it says. The voter guide explains that a "no" vote means "[a] voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature."
Groups advocating in favor of the measure include the Transparency Foundation, Latino American Political Assn, and the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association.

"Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID," their argument section says. "Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections."

Signage regarding voter identification posted outside of a polling location at the old Guilford County Courthouse during the last day of early voting in Greensboro, North Carolina, on Nov. 2, 2024. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
WATCH: BLACK BISHOP CALLS VOTER ID ARGUMENT 'DEEPLY INSULTING' AFTER EXPLOSIVE NONCITIZEN REGISTRATION REPORT
A Pew Research study released in 2025 shows that 83% of Americans back voter ID.
"It is so dark that this is the level of discourse in the OFFICIAL California voters guide," said X user Daniel Keller, who first posted a screenshot of the ballot language.
Others agreed with that sentiment, like a user named David Masten, who said: "Democracy is a farce in California."
"Good God," user Brad Pierce put it simply.
Early voting is already underway in California, as Election Day on Nov. 3 rapidly approaches.
A view of the California State Capitol on August 19, 2025, in Sacramento, California. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

If Proposition 39 is approved, the measure would require voters to present a government-issued ID when voting in person, while mail-in voters would be required to provide the last four digits of a government-issued ID number that matches the one they designated during voter registration.

It would also require election officials to use government data to verify U.S. citizenship and publish annual reports showing the percentage of registrations verified for citizenship in each county of the state. The California State Auditor would also be required to conduct regular audits of compliance with the new voter ID and citizenship requirements.
Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and California Gov. Gavin Newsom's office, but did not hear back at time of publication.
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: 'Thrill killer' and desert executioner — meet the dozens of criminals Dem AG backed for parole: 'No brainer'
summary: Aaron Ford voted to pardon or reduce sentences for 30 convicted murderers, records show, as he campaigns to unseat Gov. Joe Lombardo in Nevada.
story: Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss his closely watched race against state Attorney General Aaron Ford. Lombardo also criticizes Ford over his support for clemency in a convicted killer's case and outlines the issues shaping the race.

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford voted to support clemency for several convicted murderers, including men responsible for the kidnapping and execution-style killing of a teenager, the "thrill killing" of a Pizza Hut worker and the beating death of another victim with a cinder block.

Ford is currently facing backlash over his clemency bid for a convicted killer who took the life of a pregnant woman while out on bail for a series of armed robbery attacks on Vegas tourists. Now, a Fox News Digital review of state pardon hearings that took place during Ford's nearly eight years as attorney general show him supporting clemency for dozens of other violent offenders, with some convicted killers receiving reduced sentences, pardons or earlier parole eligibility while others had their requests denied.
Ford is running to be Nevada’s next governor, seeking to oust incumbent Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo. His race is shaping up to be one of the most competitive gubernatorial elections of the cycle.

Unlike governors in most states, Nevada's governor cannot unilaterally grant pardons or commute prison sentences, with those decisions instead resting with the state's Board of Pardons Commissioners, made up of the governor, attorney general and Nevada Supreme Court justices.
JOE LOMBARDO CRUISES PAST SIX GOP CHALLENGERS TO SECURE NEVADA REPUBLICAN GUBERNATORIAL NOMINATION

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford smiles during his governor campaign kick-off event at the East Las Vegas Community Center Monday, July 28, 2025, in Las Vegas. (Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal)
Since becoming the state’s attorney general, Ford has voted to pardon or significantly reduce the sentences of 30 people convicted of murder, Fox News Digital found.
Ford, for example, supported a convicted kidnapper and murderer eligible for parole when Lombardo voted against him.

Michael Cu, the convict in question, kidnapped a 16-year-old in 1996, forced him to drive out to the desert, then killed him execution-style — all to steal the rims off his car. The victim was shot seven times with a rifle, with the fatal shot being fired at nearly point-blank range into his head.

"Mr. Judge I would like to tell you these people, I don't want them to be free," the deceased’s mother pleaded with the judge at Cu's sentencing in March 2000. "There's a lot of people outside, a lot of mothers outside ... I'm afraid because I have more children."

Cu could eventually make it back onto the streets after the board commuted his sentence, making him eligible for parole in 2035 — though his release would still require approval from the state's parole board.
Ford has made his experience as Nevada’s top law enforcement official a focal point of his gubernatorial campaign.
ABBOTT SPOTLIGHTS NO-SHOW TALARICO, LAUNCHING TEXAS-SIZED CRIME CRACKDOWN

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford speaks during his governor campaign kick-off event at the East Las Vegas Community Center on Monday, July 28, 2025, in Las Vegas. (Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"As Attorney General, Ford has worked with federal and local law enforcement to prosecute criminals and protect our communities," his campaign website reads. "He’s gone after corporate landlords who are illegally jacking up prices, taken on big drug companies, prioritized putting child predators in jail, battled fentanyl being trafficked across our borders, and fought to keep dangerous untraceable ghost guns off of our streets. He ended a decades-long rape kit back log and has prosecuted human traffickers who threaten the safety of our communities."
Republicans may seize on some of Ford’s pardon votes to challenge the image he’s cultivated of a crusader for public safety.
While Ford offered no substantive remarks in most of the pardon hearings, he occasionally had something to add.

"I gleefully vote yes for this motion," he said, explaining his June 2022 support to make a man who killed someone in an armed robbery when he was 15 eligible for parole. Ford talked to the man, Shaquille Hazelwood, on the importance of the moment and advised him to live up to the faith the state was placing in him.

He called his decision to grant parole eligibility to an individual who stabbed a 17-year-old to death a "no-brainer" in September 2025. Ford sponsored the hearing where witnesses spoke to the character of the murderer, Bobby Thomas.

Ford also supported a commutation for Anthony Amati, whom police and prosecutors described as a "thrill killer," in a June 2025 decision that allowed the convicted murderer to become immediately eligible for parole.

Amati was convicted of ambushing a 22-year-old Pizza Hut worker as he walked a co-worker home. The co-worker, who was at the trial, testified that Amati and his friends "cackled ... laughed like it was a big joke" and jumped around while firing multiple bullets into the victim.
Deputy District Attorney Christopher Lalli argued at the time that Amati should never be eligible to walk free because his crime was a "thrill killing ... for the mere pleasure of it."
Amati became immediately eligible for parole following the board's decision, although his release was not guaranteed.
HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER
Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo secured the Republican nomination for a second term. (Mario Tama/Getty Images)

Ford also supported clemency for Arlander Givens, who beat his victim to death with a cinder block and was sentenced to two consecutive life terms, but the board ultimately denied his application, Fox News Digital found.

Other convicted killers Ford voted to grant clemency included a murderer involved in a carjacking, a man who stabbed a 17-year-old to death over a basketball game and another who lured his victim into his home with the promise of a drug deal before shooting him dead, Fox News Digital found.
GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE VOWS TO PARDON COP CONVICTED OF MANSLAUGHTER IN DEATH OF FLEEING SUSPECT

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford speaks about 2024 election security at the Clark County Election Department on Jan. 10, 2024, in North Las Vegas.  (L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Lombardo's predecessor and Ford did vote together for leniency in some cases. For instance, the duo both voted to pardon a man found guilty of masterminding a contract killing after he was exonerated by DNA evidence.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Ford’s office and his gubernatorial campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.

title: 16-year-old allegedly led ransomware gang behind hundreds of attacks
summary: Operation KillSwitch dismantled KillSec's ransomware infrastructure, but investigators say a 16-year-old allegedly ran the entire cybercrime operation.
story: Following the arrest of an alleged leader in the Netherlands, a top FBI cyber official released an unusual public address urging the remaining cybercriminals to turn themselves in "while the choice is still yours."

When you picture the person running an international ransomware operation, a 16-year-old probably does not come to mind. Yet investigators say a teenager was the suspected main operator behind KillSec, a cybercrime group linked to around 1,000 suspected attacks worldwide. About 500 of those attacks have so far been identified as successful.

Now, an international law enforcement operation has taken KillSec's leak site and key servers offline. Authorities also secured at least 110 terabytes of stolen data that could have been exposed or used to pressure victims. The takedown offers a remarkable look at how accessible cybercrime has become. More importantly, it shows how attackers continue to find their way into poorly protected systems and turn stolen files into leverage. What investigators uncovered about KillSec shows how the group operated, how AI reportedly played a role and what you can do to make ransomware attacks harder to pull off.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist.
See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com.
FBI STRIKES BACK AT HACKING GROUP WITH OVERSEAS ARREST OF ALLEGED LEADER
Guardia Civil, Mossos d’Esquadra and FBI personnel took part in the coordinated international investigation targeting KillSec. (Europol)
Police take down KillSec ransomware operation

The crackdown, known as Operation KillSwitch, took place on Sept. 30. Authorities from the United States and several European countries participated in the investigation. Europol and Eurojust also helped coordinate the effort.

Police carried out eight searches in Greece, Romania, Spain and the United Kingdom. Three suspects were provisionally arrested. Investigators also took control of five central servers connected with KillSec's operation. One of the biggest moves involved KillSec's dark web leak site. The group allegedly used the site to name victims and threaten to publish stolen files unless they paid. Authorities have now taken control of that infrastructure.
A 16-year-old is suspected of running the operation

Perhaps the most startling part of this case involves the age of the suspected operator. Investigators identified a 16-year-old as KillSec's suspected administrator and main operator. Another suspected member, described as a developer, turned 18 in August and was reportedly still a minor when some of the alleged crimes occurred.

Investigators also identified people suspected of serving as a negotiator and an affiliate. Authorities say the investigation remains ongoing. Age aside, the alleged operation was anything but small. KillSec has been active since around 2024. According to Europol, the group exploited software vulnerabilities and poorly secured access points to break into organizations. Attackers then copied sensitive internal files to systems they controlled.
How KillSec allegedly pressured its victims

Once attackers had the files, the pressure began. KillSec allegedly listed organizations on its dark web site and threatened to publish their stolen data if they refused to pay. In some cases, the stolen files were reportedly made available after victims declined to hand over a ransom.

Europol says the group received substantial ransom payments from some attacks. That strategy shows how ransomware has changed over the years. Criminals do not always need to lock every file on a computer to create leverage. Stolen information itself can become the threat. If an attacker gets employee records, customer information or confidential business documents, the victim can face serious consequences even when backups work perfectly.
KillSec reportedly used AI to support its attacks

Investigators also uncovered another detail that caught my attention. Europol says members of KillSec used artificial intelligence to help build and maintain ransomware infrastructure and identify potential victims.

That does not mean AI carried out the entire attack by itself. However, it shows how cybercriminals can use the same technology everyone else is experimenting with to speed up parts of their work. A teenager may no longer need to build every piece of an attack from scratch. Tools, stolen credentials, vulnerable systems and AI assistance can lower some of the barriers that once required deeper technical expertise. That should make all of us pay closer attention to basic security habits.
FBI'S FIRST CYBER FUGITIVE ON TEN MOST WANTED LIST RETURNS TO US AFTER CAPTURE IN VENEZUELA
Operation KillSwitch brought together international law enforcement agencies to seize KillSec’s servers, leak site and stolen data. (Felix Zahn/Photothek via Getty Images)
What happens to KillSec now?
The investigation remains active. Authorities are examining computers, servers and other seized evidence. Investigators are also following cryptocurrency and other alleged criminal proceeds.

That evidence could uncover additional attacks, victims or people connected with the operation. Europol also cautions that the current number of successful attacks may change as investigators continue reviewing what they seized.

For now, KillSec's core infrastructure has taken a significant hit. However, ransomware groups have a long history of disappearing, reorganizing and resurfacing under different names. That makes prevention especially important even after a major takedown.
Why this ransomware takedown should get your attention

KillSec appears to have focused mainly on organizations rather than individual home computer users. Still, the methods behind the attacks offer lessons that apply to everyone. Europol says the group exploited software vulnerabilities and poorly secured access points. Those are the same types of weaknesses security experts have warned about for years.

An old router, forgotten account or unpatched computer can give attackers an opening. A compromised password can do the same. Once criminals gain access, they can steal information before anyone realizes something has gone wrong. So, while you probably cannot stop an international ransomware gang yourself, you can make your devices and accounts harder to break into.
7 ways to reduce your ransomware risk
A few simple security habits can close some of the openings attackers commonly look for.

Do not keep putting off updates on your computer, phone, browser and other connected devices. Security updates often fix vulnerabilities attackers already know how to exploit. CISA recommends regularly patching operating systems and software, especially on devices exposed to the internet. Turn on automatic updates when that option is available.

Using the same password across several accounts gives an attacker more opportunities if one login is exposed. Create a different password for each important account. A password manager can help generate and store strong credentials without forcing you to remember every one. You should also check whether passwords you already use have appeared in known data leaks. Your iPhone or Android phone may already have tools that can flag compromised passwords.
HACKER CLAIMS 7.49M CUSTOMER RECORDS STOLEN FROM AMERICAN UTILITY COMPANY
Law enforcement collected laptops, phones and storage devices as evidence during the Operation KillSwitch takedown. (Europol)

A stolen password becomes much less useful when your account requires another form of verification. Enable two-factor (2FA) or multifactor authentication on your email, financial accounts, cloud storage and other important services. When available, consider phishing-resistant options such as passkeys or security keys instead of relying only on text-message codes.

Ransomware becomes far more painful when your only copy of a photo, document or financial record lives on the compromised device. Back up important files regularly. Consider keeping one copy in the cloud and another on an external drive. If you use an external drive, disconnect it when the backup finishes. Some ransomware can also target drives that remain connected to an infected computer.

A convincing email, fake update warning or malicious attachment can provide an attacker with a way into your computer. Avoid opening files you were not expecting. Instead of clicking an urgent update prompt from a webpage or email, open the app itself and check for updates there. If something feels unusual, stop before entering a password or running a downloaded file.

Strong antivirus software can help detect ransomware, malicious downloads and other threats before they spread. Keep the protection updated and run a full scan if your computer suddenly behaves differently, redirects your browser or shows unfamiliar programs. Security software will never replace safe habits. However, it can provide another opportunity to catch a threat before the damage grows. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com.

If you see a ransom message or suddenly lose access to important files, disconnect the affected device from your network. Avoid plugging backup drives into the compromised computer until you know the device is clean. The FBI says it does not support paying ransomware demands because payment does not guarantee that your information will be restored. The agency also encourages victims to report ransomware incidents. You can file a report with the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center at IC3.gov or contact your local FBI field office. The FBI specifically directs ransomware victims to use those channels. One more thing: type IC3.gov directly into your browser. The FBI has warned that scammers have created fake IC3 websites, including lookalike pages that may appear in sponsored search results.
Kurt's key takeaways

The age of KillSec's suspected operator is going to grab the headlines, and I understand why. Sixteen is incredibly young to be accused of running an operation connected with this many attacks. What stays with me, though, is how familiar the alleged entry points sound. Vulnerable software and poorly protected access can still give criminals exactly the opening they need. That is why I keep coming back to the basics. Update your devices. Protect important accounts with more than a password. Keep a backup that an attacker cannot easily reach. You may never know which security step stopped an attack. That is far better than discovering which one you skipped after your files are already gone.

If a 16-year-old can allegedly help run a ransomware operation tied to hundreds of successful attacks, do you think powerful hacking tools and AI are making cybercrime too easy to enter at a young age? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

Keeping it all running, however, takes an army of electricians, mechanics, technicians and construction workers — and the industry says it needs more of them.
