Rep. Tom Barrett, R-Mich., wrote on X that “Secretary Hegseth should seriously reconsider this decision.”

Other Republican lawmakers have signaled support for the livestream plan. On Saturday, Rep. Matt Van Epps, R-Tenn., told NBC News that “Parents should not let their kids watch that. Just like they should have good parental guidance for social media and other things. This administration is focused on accountability.”

Earlier in the day on Truth Social, Trump reposted a Dallas Morning News article in which Robert Jeffress, a prominent Trump ally and the senior pastor of First Baptist Dallas, said that he supports the plan for a public killing.

title: Mail ballot concerns are changing how Democrats vote
summary: Democrats are changing how they vote, requesting fewer mail ballots than in past elections but returning the ones they do request more quickly, according to a new NBC News Decision Desk analysis of the early vote conducted in coordination with the University of Pennsylvania.
story: Democrats are changing how they vote, requesting fewer mail ballots than in past elections but returning the ones they do request more quickly, according to a new NBC News Decision Desk analysis of the early vote conducted in coordination with the University of Pennsylvania.

The findings, which come less than four weeks before Election Day, reflect a midterm landscape shaped by concerns about mail-in voting and doubts about the reliability of the U.S. Postal Service. The shift among Democrats suggests they may be abandoning mail ballots in favor of in-person voting, or taking precautions to ensure their ballot arrives on time.

The implications could be significant. Since 2020, Democrats have been far more likely than Republicans to vote by mail, creating predictable patterns in how early election tallies shift as additional votes are counted. But if those habits are changing, it will be more difficult to gauge which party has more enthusiasm from early voting figures, while the now-familiar red and blue “mirages” seen on recent election nights could unfold differently.

For the analysis, we compared current and historical data on mail ballot requests and returns at the same point in time across four states: North Carolina, Georgia, Virginia and Pennsylvania. We gathered publicly available data from three states and sourced Virginia data from L2, a leading voter data firm.
Trump order supercharges concerns about the Postal Service

President Donald Trump has long attacked mail voting as rife with unfounded claims of fraud. Heading into the midterms, his administration exerted increased control over the Postal Service, whose slowed delivery times had already prompted voting rights groups and Democrats to push their voters to consider using other methods of voting.

Just months before the first mail ballots of the midterm elections were scheduled to go out, the Postal Service followed a Trump directive to impose new rules about how election officials could send those ballots to voters. The new requirements will ultimately not apply to this year’s midterm election, but the high-profile legal battle magnified worries about the reliability of the Postal Service.

Confidence that the Postal Service would deliver mail ballots on time plummeted among Democrats from 86% before the 2024 election to 60% now, according to polling conducted by Marist in September, just after the Supreme Court blocked the new Postal Service rules from going into effect. Confidence among Republicans remains unchanged. Meanwhile, more Democrats said they planned to vote in person this year than said the same at this time in 2024, according to NBC News polling.
The early vote data we examined suggests that what these Democratic voters may actually do is dependent on when voters may request mail ballots in each state.

In some states, voters may join a permanent list of mail voters or an annual list at the start of each year. If voters could request their ballot long before concerns about the Postal Service became national news, Democrats are still voting by mail, but taking steps to get those ballots back to election officials more quickly, the analysis shows.
But if Democrats face the choice about whether to request a mail ballot only after the Postal Service challenges, it’s more likely that ballot requests are down from previous election years.
Changing early voting patterns

In North Carolina, where the Senate race is poised to help decide control of the chamber, registrants typically apply for a mail ballot in the months before each particular election. As a result, few individuals had requested mail ballots for the upcoming midterm before the Postal Service attempted to impose its new rules.

So far, Democrats in the state are both less likely to request and more likely to return mail ballots compared to 2022, the most recent midterm election year. The decrease is larger among Democratic registered voters at 40% than among Republican registered voters or independent or third-party registrants at 18% and 23%, respectively. Further, the Democratic registrants who have requested mail ballots are more likely to have already returned them in 2026 (22%) than in 2022 (17%).

In Georgia, a state with competitive Senate and gubernatorial contests and a similar mail ballot request policy, we see the same pattern. While it’s not possible to directly replicate the North Carolina analysis because registrants in the state do not declare a party of registration and domestic mail ballots only went out this week, we can use how each precinct voted in 2024 as an approximation of the partisanship of voters.

As in North Carolina, the analysis shows that mail ballot requests are down more in precincts that overwhelmingly supported Kamala Harris (52%) than in precincts that overwhelmingly supported Donald Trump (39%).

The story is different in Virginia. Unlike North Carolina or Georgia, Virginia allows registrants to sign up for a permanent absentee mailing list, and a substantial share of returned mail ballots are cast by registered voters on this permanent list. As a result, there’s been no drop-off in mail ballot requests compared to the last general election held in the state.

But as in Georgia and North Carolina, Democrats are returning their mail ballots faster. In the most Democratic precincts, 69% more ballots were returned at this point in the 2026 election compared to 2025, compared to 5% fewer returned ballots in the most Republican precincts.
One advantage of analyzing Virginia is that it is one of the few states with a significant amount of early in-person voting at this point in the electoral calendar.

Relative to 2025, there are more early in-person ballots already cast in precincts that overwhelmingly supported Harris (+10%) in 2024 than in precincts that overwhelmingly supported Trump (-14%). But only a small portion of this increase is caused by people shifting from voting by mail to voting early in person, so it does not explain most of the increase in early in-person voting.
For Subscribers

Still, the relatively higher rate of people voting early in person in Democratic precincts compared to Republican precincts suggests that most Democrats who are shifting away from mail balloting, including in North Carolina and Georgia, may move to voting in person rather than not voting at all.

Finally, consider Pennsylvania, which maintains an annual list for mail ballot applications. Of the four states analyzed, it had the highest share of ballots cast by mail in the 2024 presidential election — 27%, versus Virginia at 11%, North Carolina at 5% and Georgia at 5%.

When registrants request a mail ballot in Pennsylvania, they are permitted to request a mail ballot for every subsequent election in that calendar year. Many registrants who request a mail ballot for the May primary election also request a mail ballot for the upcoming general election.

As in North Carolina and Georgia, there are fewer mail ballot requests from Democrats at this point in 2026 than in 2022. However, there is no difference among Democrats requesting mail ballots by May. Instead, the decline is concentrated among mail ballot requests after May, likely reflecting the increased uncertainty about the Postal Service since the summer.

Further, consistent with the other findings, Democrats are returning their mail ballots faster than in the past. A higher percentage of mail ballots requested by registered Democrats have already been returned (20%) than at this same point in 2022 (15%).
Why changing voting habits could complicate election night analysis

These changes in Democratic voting behavior present two challenges for election analysts: determining what the early vote data reveal about voter enthusiasm, and understanding what’s happening on election night as results are processed.
At this point, it is difficult to use the initial mail ballot data to gauge each party’s likelihood of success.
For Subscribers

The relative decline in mail ballot requests could be interpreted as a sign that Democrats have less momentum heading into the midterm election than current polling indicates. But Democrats may also be shifting from voting by mail to voting in person, as the findings in Virginia suggest.

Conversely, the relative increase in mail ballot returns among Democrats might mean the party’s voters are particularly enthusiastic about the upcoming election. But this pattern is also consistent with these Democrats returning their mail ballots faster to address concerns about Postal Service slowdowns.

Observing who casts early in-person votes over the next several weeks will help test these competing narratives. Still, we won’t have a clear picture of voter enthusiasm until we see who turns out on Election Day.
Beyond that, our findings underscore the need for caution when interpreting early voting data and election-night results.

Analysts often rely on voting patterns from past elections as key benchmarks to assess how each party is performing on election night. But if more Democrats vote in person, or get those mail ballots in faster, the timing of when Democratic votes are reported and counted could change in important ways. Thus, what may seem to be either a Democratic over- or under- performance on election night could instead be the reflection of the election landscape shifting once more.

title: MAHA fractures deepen as some RFK Jr. followers turn into harsh critics
summary: A scorecard from MAHA activists suggests the Trump administration has broken most of its promises to the movement. The “burn feels especially raw,” one prominent activist said.
story: Some supporters of the “Make America Healthy Again” movement have begun to publicly turn against their leader, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and the Trump administration as a whole as they demand tougher crackdowns on food dyes and pesticides.

A scorecard released Thursday by MAHA activists, including former members of Kennedy’s 2024 presidential campaign, claims the Trump administration broke more than 85% of its promises to MAHA on food, agriculture and environmental health. The makers of the scorecard include Dave Murphy, a former fundraiser for Kennedy’s campaign, and Charles Eisenstein, Kennedy’s former chief speechwriter.

NBC News is first to report on the scorecard, which offers a window into how MAHA views the administration, and Kennedy himself, ahead of the midterm elections. It accuses the Trump administration of doling out favors to the chemical industry, pointing to its decision to approve new pesticides and hire industry lobbyists and executives.

“We’re asking the Trump administration to deliver on even the most basic promises they’ve made to the MAHA movement, and we’ve seen over and over again not just a lack of interest in doing so, but a blatant slap in the face,” said former Kennedy campaign adviser Tiffany Cianci, a MAHA advocate who authored the scorecard.

About 41% of adults in the U.S. say they support MAHA ideals, according to an April poll from KFF, a nonprofit health think tank. Most are Republicans or Republican-leaning independents, according to the poll, though alignment with Kennedy or President Donald Trump wasn’t a primary reason for supporting the movement.

MAHA coalesced during Kennedy’s presidential bid in 2024, then threw its support behind Trump when Kennedy endorsed him. It brought together multiple social movements, including food safety, environmentalism and vaccine skepticism, under the umbrella of taking on big corporations whose products may contribute to chronic diseases.
But many of these advocates have become Kennedy’s harshest critics as of late, arguing that their priorities are being ignored by the Trump administration.

Covid vaccine skeptics such as Dr. Mary Talley Bowden have criticized Kennedy and Trump for allowing mRNA vaccines to stay on the market. Food safety advocates say Kennedy hasn’t put enough pressure on companies to remove synthetic dyes and other additives from their products. And advocates for reducing pesticide exposure claim Trump undermined their mission by issuing an executive order to boost the supply of the weed killer glyphosate in the U.S.
That dissatisfaction has led to infighting between Kennedy loyalists — including those appointed to key government positions — and activists faithful to their original cause.

“What started out as a hairline crack in the coalition is now widened to be a gaping fissure,” said Peter Lurie, president of the Center for Science in the Public Interest, a nonprofit advocacy group focused on nutrition and food safety.

White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said the Trump administration “has already secured extensive victories for the MAHA Agenda, including overhauling the dietary guidelines for Americans, axing artificial ingredients in our food supply, and investing in regenerative farming.”

“After years of being on the political sidelines, the MAHA coalition has found a champion in President Trump, who has made incredible strides to Make America Healthy Again,” Schuster said in a statement.
Emily Hilliard, a spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, said Kennedy “remains focused on delivering lasting reforms grounded in science, transparency, and accountability.”

“President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are delivering the fundamental change Americans voted for. In just 20 months, this Administration has moved at a historic pace to advance MAHA across the federal government,” she said in a statement.

Cianci acknowledged that many of the administration’s actions on environmental toxins and food additives have been outside of Kennedy’s purview. But his time in the administration has done “obvious harm” to his reputation, she said, noting that Kennedy’s career history involved suing the very pharmaceutical and pesticide companies the administration is now working with.

“To see him not speaking out on the issues that are so obviously against everything that was promised is very hard because I believe ethically it’s probably working against his own inclinations,” Cianci said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Kelly Ryerson, a well-known MAHA advocate who goes by the moniker “Glyphosate Girl” and helped develop the scorecard, said she doesn’t fault Kennedy as much as the rest of Trump’s Cabinet because she knows “where his heart lies.”

“I know how deep the forces are in terms of corporate influence on regulators, and it’s something that he himself has criticized for years,” she said. “[But] the actions of the administration have worked really in opposition to everything that we hoped and everything that Trump promised.”

Pamela Herd, a professor of social policy at the University of Michigan, said the MAHA movement was always vulnerable to conflict because it consists of unusual bedfellows: liberal moms who feed their kids organic produce, fringe doctors who falsely claim that vaccines cause autism and Trump supporters who want to remove corporate influence from the federal government.

Over time, though, MAHA’s main goals have solidified. A March poll from Politico suggests that removing ultra-processed foods from American diets and limiting exposure to PFAS, microplastics and pesticides were key priorities for people who self-identified as part of the movement.
“What the MAHA movement has always been especially interested in is chemicals,” Lurie said.

Much of Cianci’s scorecard focuses on actions taken by the Environmental Protection Agency and Agriculture Department — agencies Kennedy does not oversee. For instance, it considers the EPA’s decisions to weaken mercury emissions standards and roll back drinking water limits for certain PFAS as broken promises.
Phasing out food dyes
Several of the promises that were “partially kept,” according to the scorecard, come directly from Kennedy-led agencies like the Food and Drug Administration.

For instance, the FDA asked food companies to voluntarily phase out certain dyes and banned two others that were not widely used. It also proposed a requirement for food manufacturers to notify the FDA when they determine that an additive is “generally recognized as safe.” The rule would not remove the additives already in food or prevent manufacturers from adding more, however.

Lurie said Kennedy campaigned on fixing these issues, but “never took into account the practical aspects on the ground: What do the regulations actually look like? What authority do these agencies actually have?”

The scorecard does not mention an action Kennedy has touted often: his January overhaul of the federal dietary guidelines, which encourages Americans to eat more protein and cut out ultra-processed foods.

It also does not address Kennedy’s vaccination policies. Both Kennedy and Trump have attempted to reduce the number of universally recommended vaccines for children. And Kennedy last year fired the longtime members of a federal vaccine advisory committee, replacing them with vaccine skeptics. (A federal judge temporarily blocked the change, which is still being challenged in court.)
“If you’re going to pick one thing that RFK was successful at, it’s very much how he has influenced government policy on vaccines,” Herd, the University of Michigan professor, said.
Kennedy reassured anti-vaccine activists last month that they have “a strong and steadfast friend at the White House.”
But as tensions mount, many MAHA supporters insist the movement does not need a political affiliation. Ryerson said MAHA voters will likely sit out the upcoming midterm elections.

“The disappointments with Obama and Biden are similar to the disappointments with Trump,” she said. “The difference with this administration is that we are promised something very, very different in a very real way, so I think that that burn feels especially raw.”

title: Trump says Nobel committee not awarding him Peace Prize leaves ‘indelible stain’ on Norway
summary: President Donald Trump lamented that the Norwegian Nobel Committee chose not to award him with its annual Peace Prize on Friday, telling rallygoers the decision leaves “an indelible stain on the country of Norway.”
story: President Donald Trump lamented that the Norwegian Nobel Committee chose not to award him with its annual Peace Prize on Friday, telling rallygoers the decision leaves “an indelible stain on the country of Norway.”

Speaking at a rally in Syracuse to boost New York Republicans, Trump listed off all of the accomplishments he believes have earned him the right to win the Nobel Peace Prize, including efforts to end or prevent conflicts in Africa and Asia and for having “saved more lives than anyone in history.”
Earlier Friday, the committee awarded the prize to Navi Pillay, an 85-year-old South African legal pioneer who led a United Nations panel that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

“I’ve never heard of the person,” Trump said. “I know a lot of people. I never heard of this particular person, but congratulations, anyway. … The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t.”

“And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump continued. “The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are antidemocracy and really enemies of civilization, and we will not forget Norway, that you didn’t give this prize with the greatest record in history.”

The president added that he should have received eight Nobel Peace Prizes for his efforts because he claimed to have ended eight ongoing conflicts. The president did not mention the war in Ukraine, which has raged on through his presidency as his administration has failed to bring the conflict to an end. And in the Middle East, the president earlier this year launched an ongoing war with Iran.
Trump said the committee’s choice to award the prize to Pillay “is just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country.”

Throughout his second term, the president has made clear his ambition to secure a Nobel Peace Prize, and his allies have said he deserves it for efforts to end the war in Gaza in addition to other conflicts. Earlier this year, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, the 2025 winner, offered to share her prize with him as she sought his support for her efforts in Venezuela after the Trump administration removed President Nicolás Maduro from power.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
After learning of her award at a law gathering in Germany on Friday, Pillay joked to the crowd: “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.”

The president was in Syracuse to boost the candidacy of GOP gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman and state Republicans. He shouted out Saritha Komatireddy, the Republican nominee for state attorney general too, before attacking sitting state Attorney General Letitia James, a Democrat he has often clashed with.
“And on Election Day, New Yorkers should tell both [Gov. Kathy] Hochul and that disgusting Letitia dog — she’s a dog — you’re fired, get the hell out of here.”

The Trump administration has so far failed multiple times in its efforts to prosecute James, who spearheaded an investigation into his business dealings that led to a state judge ruling he had conspired to manipulate his net worth and ordering him to pay a fine of more than $350 million. The fine was later thrown out on appeal by a state court.

“Donald Trump is in Syracuse supporting the only attorney general candidate who clerked for Brett Kavanaugh, the man who ended Roe v. Wade,” a James campaign spokesperson said in response to the president’s comments. “The contrast is crystal clear and we welcome it.”

title: Deal alert: Walmart’s has AirPods 4 for $79
summary: Walmart has Apple AirPods 4 on sale for $79, down from $130. That’s lower than the price during Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days. Here’s what to know.
story: If you held off on buying AirPods during Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, your patience just paid off. Walmart has Apple AirPods 4 on sale for $79 right now, which is even lower than the price they dropped to during Amazon’s sale. title: Second defendant in Cornell fraternity case seeks New York AG’s recusal
summary: Attorneys representing Winston Lee, one of the former fraternity members accused in the Cornell University sexual assault lawsuit, filed a motion Friday in criminal court seeking to disqualify New York Attorney General Letitia James from any future grand jury proceedings.
story: Attorneys representing Winston Lee, one of the former fraternity members accused in the Cornell University sexual assault lawsuit, filed a motion Friday in criminal court seeking to disqualify New York Attorney General Letitia James from any future grand jury proceedings.

The motion — filed by attorneys Teny Geragos, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan — asked a judge to preclude James from conducting a criminal investigation into whether former Chi Phi members, including Lee, engaged in sexual assault in October 2024.

Lee’s attorneys argued that the Tompkins County court has the authority to step in if necessary to ensure the fairness of a grand jury process. They are asking for any future potential grand jury panelists to be polled on whether they are aware of James’ comments. They also asked for the court to schedule arguments on the issue.

In response to a request for comment, a spokesperson for James’ office said: “In this and every investigation, the Office of the Attorney General is committed to conducting a comprehensive review of nothing but the facts, the evidence, and the law.”

The filing follows a separate legal effort by lawyers for Cornell defendant Gillio Lopes, who earlier this week filed a civil court motion asking a judge for the same relief: the dismissal of James following her appointment as special counsel by Gov. Kathy Hochul.

Jane Doe’s civil suit was filed last month against seven fraternity members as well as Cornell, the Chi Phi fraternity and her sorority. The lawsuit alleges that both Lee and Lopes did drugs off her body and sexually assaulted her. Lee’s and Lopes’ attorneys say their clients deny the accusations brought against them.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Two of the other men named in the suit have also denied separate allegations against them. None of the men named has been criminally charged. Cornell has said that it welcomes new investigations into the case. The fraternity and sorority previously declined to discuss the pending litigation.

It also marks the first time the well-known legal team, which has handled a number of significant sexual misconduct matters, publicly acknowledged representing one of the men accused by a former Cornell student who filed a lawsuit last month under the pseudonym Jane Doe.

Hochul and James “have together created a blatant appearance of impropriety that, combined with the AG’s ethical violations, should lead to the AG’s recusal,” Geragos wrote in a motion filed in criminal court in Tompkins County, the upstate New York area where Cornell is located.
Geragos pointed to social media comments posted by James as Jane Doe’s lawsuit captured national attention.

“What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable,” James wrote prior to her appointment as special prosecutor. “To her and all other survivors: You’re not alone. We stand with you.”

Lawyers for Lee and Lopes argue the remarks show that James prejudged the case and is unfit to conduct an impartial review of the matter. An Oct. 29 hearing has been set in Lopes’ case for James’ office to argue that her appointment should not be voided.
For Subscribers
“The public needs confidence that the person directing this investigation will evaluate the evidence with an open mind,” Lopes’ attorney, Andrew Miltenberg, said in a statement on Friday.
For Subscribers
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten vowed to present evidence to a grand jury prior to James’ office taking on the probe.

Van Houten previously found that Jane Doe had not described a prosecutable crime in a six-page statement provided to police in November 2024 and ruled out the possibility of charges. Jane Doe told police that she engaged in a consensual threesome on the evening in question, but that events spiraled as she became increasingly incapacitated and more men became involved.

Thomas Giuffra, an attorney for Jane Doe, has previously said that sex assault victims sometimes do not immediately recognize the coercive nature of an encounter because they rationalize aspects of a traumatic event.
Geragos’ law firm, Agnifilo Intrater LLP, previously represented hip-hop mogul Sean “Diddy” Combs and Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein in high-profile criminal trials.

Combs, 56, was acquitted in July 2025 on one count of racketeering conspiracy and two counts of sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion. The jury found him guilty on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. The rapper and record producer was sentenced to 50 months in federal prison.
The jury in Weinstein’s third trial failed to reach a unanimous verdict on a third-degree rape charge involving Jessica Mann, a former aspiring actor. The judge declared a mistrial in May.

In a separate trial last year, the former Miramax chief was convicted on a count of first-degree criminal sexual act involving Miriam “Mimi” Haley, a former “Project Runway” production assistant. He was recently sentenced to 15 years in prison.

Marc Agnifilo and his wife, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, represent Luigi Mangione, the 28-year-old accused of fatally shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Mangione in August pleaded not guilty to federal stalking charges, kicking off a double jeopardy fight in New York state court, where he still faces murder charges.

title: DHS officials defend their actions in shooting of NYC immigrant amid outcry
summary: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the man shot, Oscar Bergal for endangering the life of the child, who was seating in the backseat of Belgal’s car.
story: Senior Homeland Security officials defended the ICE officers involved in the shooting of a Dominican man in New York City on Thursday, which happened in the presence of his 5-year-old son.
DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the man who was shot, Oscar Bergal, for endangering the life of the child, who was seating in the back seat of Bergal’s car.

“We weren’t aware the child was in the car. I can tell you that, but you know who was? Oscar. Oscar knew he had a child in his car,” Mullin said in a news briefing Friday at ICE’s headquarters in Washington, D.C.

According to a timeline of events provided during the briefing, ICE officers tried to arrest Bergal, 28, using two vehicles to block his car. After he refused orders to exit his car, Bergal accelerated and smashed into the ICE vehicles.
Executive Associate Director of Enforcement and Removal Operations Marcos Charles said Bergal “weaponized his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate, going towards other officers.”
The officers responded by firing their weapons, believing “that their life and the life of the partners and general public were in danger,” he added.
Bergal stopped his car after he was “struck by one of the bullets or fragments superficially in the neck,” Charles said. “We arrested him, rendered first aid, and then took him to the hospital.”

Body-camera footage from New York Police Department officers who responded to the shooting shows they were the ones who transported Bergal to the hospital to receive medical care. The NYPD has said it was not involved in Bergal’s immigration arrest.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
As of Thursday night, Bergal was in stable condition, according to NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch.

The incident has sparked public outcry in New York City, with Mayor Zohran Mamdani saying on Thursday night that “there is no explanation for federal officers firing this many rounds into a car that has a 5-year-old in the car.”
Protests erupted shortly after the shooting in Marble Hill, with five people taken into custody Thursday night, according to the NYPD. More protests are expected on Friday evening.
During the briefing, Mullin said that outrage should be directed “towards this criminal” and not his agency.

According to authorities, Bergal was previously arrested for robbery, for which he pleaded guilty to fourth-degree grand larceny and received five years’ probation. He also has a pending case for criminal sale of a controlled substance.

Mullin said they were “serving a lawful warrant” when ICE officers arrested Bergal on Thursday. In a habeas petition filed by Bergal’s attorneys seeking his release from immigration custody and obtained by NBC News, his attorneys alleged ICE officers “lacked a valid warrant for Mr. Bergal’s arrest.”
Bergal did not appear at a court hearing Friday afternoon. While he wasn’t required to be present in this first hearing, several family members were there, sitting in the front row.

Paige Austin, one of Bergal’s lawyers, said her client still has a bullet in his body and hasn’t been able to speak to his family. He has been booked into the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn.
Charles said Bergal evaded officers last month when ICE tried to arrest him for deportation.
The ICE shooting in New York City coincided with another immigration enforcement incident on Thursday in Harrison, New Jersey, which also took place in the presence of children.

DHS told NBC News in a statement that ICE officers were seeking to arrest Jhon Maykel Correa-Sangucho, a Honduran national they say is not authorized to be in the country and has multiple traffic infractions.

A video of the arrest filmed by a bystander shows two children screaming as they cling to a man ICE officers are detaining. A woman is also taken into custody. The two weeping young children are seen collapsed on the sidewalk, howling as they see agents complete the arrest and drive away.
DHS said Correa-Sangucho was inside his car and had declined multiple orders to exit his vehicle during that encounter, but ICE officers were able to remove him from the car.
The woman who was with Correa-Sangucho and a bystander “attempted to obstruct the arrest,” DHS said, adding they are “under investigation for assaulting, resisting, and impeding federal officers.”

The video did not show any conversation on whether the adults could take the children with them to enter family detention. NBC News asked Mullin at the news conference what the plans were for the children.
“We’ll give them an option to allow the kids to go with them once the scene is secured,” Mullin said.

title: Country star Ella Langley cancels Tulsa, Oklahoma, show due to ‘serious security threat’
summary: Country singer Ella Langley canceled Friday’s sold-out show in Tulsa, Oklahoma, due to what she described as “a serious security threat.”
story: Country singer Ella Langley canceled Friday’s sold-out show in Tulsa, Oklahoma, due to what she described as “a serious security threat.”
The 27-year-old star announced the last-minute cancellation on Instagram, saying the threat involved “the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team.”
“The incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show,” she said. “This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team.”
Tulsa police said Friday “a call was made threatening the lives of people attending the event.”

Police swept the area with its K-9 unit, bomb team, patrol officers and venue security but did not find anything dangerous, and the building and surrounding area was swept a second time, but police “again found no credible threat to the event’s safety,” the department said.
Police said they advised Langley’s staff that no credible threat was found, “but they decided to cancel the performance anyway.”

“We apologize to everyone who came down tonight. We appreciate your patience, and it is unfortunate that some nefarious characters successfully disrupted the event, ruining the evening for thousands of people,” police said.
The incident remains under investigation.
Langley — whose single “Choosin’ Texas” has made history for topping the Billboard Hot 100 for over 23 weeks — apologized to her fans, but stressed safety is paramount.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am. This is not a decision that was made lightly,” she said.
“I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way,” she continued.
The show was set to take place at Tulsa’s BOK Center, which shared the same statement Langley included in her social media post.

“The safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed,” the statement said. “The safety of fans is our foremost concern and will always come first.”
The statement said details regarding refunds will be shared soon.

title: USS Lincoln docks in San Diego Bay following scrutinized 322-day deployment
summary: Families of crewmembers arrived hours ahead of the carrier’s return after reported suicide attempts, dwindling supplies and harsh conditions became synonymous with its deployment.
story: ABOARD THE USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN — Draped in red, white and blue striped banners, the USS Abraham Lincoln arrived in San Diego Bay after 322 days at sea. It ended one of the longest maritime deployments in U.S. military history, returning home to eager loved ones, as well as ongoing scrutiny over past reports of low morale.
Elated crewmembers lined the decks portside — some waved to the waiting crowds, and others danced as their loved ones cheered from below.
“It’s a combination of the day before Christmas and the last day of school,” the commanding officer, Capt. Dan Keeler, told NBC News, adding that some of the crewmembers are just 18 years old.
“They are amazing, you know, legends and heroes,” he said. “Every single one of them.”
Among the first to depart at the Naval Air Station North Island in Coronado will be 64 parents who have been waiting months to meet their babies for the first time, The Associated Press reported.
USS Lincoln sailor will meet his baby boy when ship docks

Sailor Brent Ledbetter told NBC News that he has watched his son grow via videos and photos sent by his wife, an air traffic control officer who was also assigned to the ship. She was relieved of duty because of her pregnancy.
“I just want to hold him, play with him,” Ledbetter said.

The Lincoln’s return to Coronado caps off more than 10 months of the ship’s engagement in the Middle East. It was deployed as part of the U.S.’ war with Iran. The aircraft carrier drew national attention over reports of supply shortages and at least eight suicide attempts.

It was at sea without a port call for 286 days, the second-longest deployment since the Vietnam War, and surpassed 300 consecutive days overseas overall. The USS Gerald R. Ford set the record for longest deployment by an aircraft carrier at 326 days, which ended this year, the AP reported.
Families and loved ones of crewmembers arrived hours ahead of the carrier’s return Thursday, waiting in line to get on the naval base near San Diego.
The Lincoln and its air wing dropped more than 1,145 weapons in its 10 months at sea. Some of the crew painted a mural depicting the 1,463 objects hit during the operation.

title: Trump says Nobel committee not awarding him Peace Prize leaves ‘indelible stain’ on Norway
summary: President Donald Trump lamented that the Norwegian Nobel Committee chose not to award him with its annual Peace Prize on Friday, telling rallygoers the decision leaves “an indelible stain on the country of Norway.”
story: President Donald Trump lamented that the Norwegian Nobel Committee chose not to award him with its annual Peace Prize on Friday, telling rallygoers the decision leaves “an indelible stain on the country of Norway.”

Speaking at a rally in Syracuse to boost New York Republicans, Trump listed off all of the accomplishments he believes have earned him the right to win the Nobel Peace Prize, including efforts to end or prevent conflicts in Africa and Asia and for having “saved more lives than anyone in history.”
Earlier Friday, the committee awarded the prize to Navi Pillay, an 85-year-old South African legal pioneer who led a United Nations panel that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

“I’ve never heard of the person,” Trump said. “I know a lot of people. I never heard of this particular person, but congratulations, anyway. … The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t.”

“And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump continued. “The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are antidemocracy and really enemies of civilization, and we will not forget Norway, that you didn’t give this prize with the greatest record in history.”

The president added that he should have received eight Nobel Peace Prizes for his efforts because he claimed to have ended eight ongoing conflicts. The president did not mention the war in Ukraine, which has raged on through his presidency as his administration has failed to bring the conflict to an end. And in the Middle East, the president earlier this year launched an ongoing war with Iran.
Trump said the committee’s choice to award the prize to Pillay “is just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country.”

Throughout his second term, the president has made clear his ambition to secure a Nobel Peace Prize, and his allies have said he deserves it for efforts to end the war in Gaza in addition to other conflicts. Earlier this year, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, the 2025 winner, offered to share her prize with him as she sought his support for her efforts in Venezuela after the Trump administration removed President Nicolás Maduro from power.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
After learning of her award at a law gathering in Germany on Friday, Pillay joked to the crowd: “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.”

The president was in Syracuse to boost the candidacy of GOP gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman and state Republicans. He shouted out Saritha Komatireddy, the Republican nominee for state attorney general too, before attacking sitting state Attorney General Letitia James, a Democrat he has often clashed with.
“And on Election Day, New Yorkers should tell both [Gov. Kathy] Hochul and that disgusting Letitia dog — she’s a dog — you’re fired, get the hell out of here.”

The Trump administration has so far failed multiple times in its efforts to prosecute James, who spearheaded an investigation into his business dealings that led to a state judge ruling he had conspired to manipulate his net worth and ordering him to pay a fine of more than $350 million. The fine was later thrown out on appeal by a state court.

“Donald Trump is in Syracuse supporting the only attorney general candidate who clerked for Brett Kavanaugh, the man who ended Roe v. Wade,” a James campaign spokesperson said in response to the president’s comments. “The contrast is crystal clear and we welcome it.”

title: AIPAC’s super PAC starts spending again in the Michigan Senate race
summary: A super PAC tied to the pro-Israel group AIPAC has resumed spending in Michigan’s critical Senate race, funding new mailers targeting Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, according to a new campaign finance report.
story: A super PAC tied to the pro-Israel group AIPAC has resumed spending in Michigan’s critical Senate race, funding new mailers targeting Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, according to a new campaign finance report.

The group, United Democracy Project, hadn’t been involved in the general election despite spending millions to oppose El-Sayed, a vocal critic of Israel, in the Democratic primary in August. The group filed a report with the Federal Election Commission on Friday showing that it spent $95,000 on mailers opposing El-Sayed.

The group is targeting 130,000 Jewish voters with mailers, according to spokesperson Patrick Dorton. The mailer features a headline about an attack on a Michigan synagogue in March, which the FBI described as an “Hezbollah-inspired act of terrorism.”

“Abdul El-Sayed’s response: ‘Hurt people hurt people,’” the mailer reads, according to a copy shared with NBC News. El-Sayed apologized in late August for his response to the attack, saying his comments “may have been misconstrued to justify something I did not mean to justify.”

The new spending is just a fraction of the $33 million United Democracy Project spent on ads in the Democratic primary against El-Sayed and in support of his primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. Stevens is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed has accused Israel of committing a genocide in Gaza.
El-Sayed is now facing off against former GOP Rep. Mike Rogers, who has slammed his opponent for his positions on Israel.

During their first debate Thursday night, Rogers said he would welcome AIPAC’s involvement when asked about an Axios report that the former congressman’s allies had asked the group to stay out of the race.
For Subscribers

“Anybody that wants to help my campaign stop a guy who can’t condemn terrorism in our own country because he’s so close to the people who are supporting the Muslim Brotherhood, again, I’ll take all of that help,” Rogers said. El-Sayed interjected to say, “Again, I’ve condemned them.”
El-Sayed was asked during the debate whether he would support funding for defensive weapons for Israel if the country were attacked.
“I don’t want our tax dollars buying weapons for other countries. I don’t know what’s so hard about that,” El-Sayed responded.
He was also whether Iran or Israel posed a bigger threat to the United States, and declined to answer, calling the question “a ridiculous hypothetical.”
For Subscribers

“I don’t want to be pushed into war by Israel, and I don’t want to be in a war with Iran,” El-Sayed said. “I want our money spent here to buy schools and healthcare and childcare here. I don’t understand why that is so inconceivable.”

Rogers, speaking to reporters at a campaign event Friday night in Highland Township, Michigan, noted that the expenditure was relatively small but suggested it would nonetheless get under El-Sayed’s skin.
“This tells you something that you need to know about my opponent: He is so anti-Jewish that one mail piece sends him into orbit,” Rogers said.
Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., who appeared with Rogers at two events Friday, then jumped in to attack El-Sayed in more explicit terms.
“Look, AIPAC wouldn’t come here if Dr. El-Sayed didn’t sleep in a Bin Laden jersey,” Kennedy said.
Pressed by NBC News to explain the comment, Kennedy said: “He supports Hamas. He’s antisemitic. He hates Israel. He doesn’t feel gratitude for America.”

El-Sayed has condemned Hamas as “evil,” while also describing the Israeli government the same way. Rogers also repeatedly accused El-Sayed of supporting Hamas during the two candidates’ debate on Thursday.

El-Sayed responded in his closing statement by saying, “Look, I told you what this debate was going to be: him pointing at me and saying all kinds of foreign names, or him talking about himself. And I told you I’m interested in you.”

title: James Talarico back on the trail after absence with flu drew scrutiny
summary: After drawing scrutiny for his absence from the campaign trail, Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico, who had been sick with the flu, returned to the stump.
story: After drawing scrutiny for his absence from the campaign trail, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, who had been sick with the flu, returned to the stump in Texas on Friday.
“James Talarico is back on the campaign trail talking to voters at Austin City Limits,” Talarico campaign spokesman JT Ennis said in a statement.
Social media posts showed Talarico walking on the grounds of the festival on Friday.

Talarico revealed on Sept. 30 that he was sick, when he had to appear virtually instead of in person at a forum. His prolonged absence drew daily scrutiny from his opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Paxton’s campaign asked for “proof of life” and called on Talarico to produce a photo of himself and a newspaper with a current date. Republican Sen. Ted Cruz poked fun on social media, featuring a milk carton with Talarico’s face with the word “MISSING.”

Talarico’s last in-person event in the state was on Sept. 26. He visited New York on Sept. 29 for a private fundraiser and, according to his virtual remarks to the Hispanic Business Council the following day, he returned to Dallas and visited urgent care.
For Subscribers
Then, Talarico appeared visibly ill, blowing his nose and coughing through the event.
For Subscribers

“I was starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago, and last night it got so bad that I went to the urgent care here in Dallas, and I was diagnosed with the flu,” Talarico said at the time. “I’m running a fever, and I’m my most contagious right now. And I guess I’ve been shaking too many hands on the campaign trail, and so I want to keep everybody safe.”
His absence from the trail in the crunch time of the election prompted some consternation among Democrats.
“Believe me, we don’t want this right now,” a Texas Democrat involved in the Talarico race said. “We’d rather have him on the trail.”

title: Mike Ditka, legendary Chicago Bears coach, dies at 86
summary: Legendary Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka, who led the team to its only Super Bowl victory in 1986, has died, his family announced.
story: Legendary Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka, who led the team to its only Super Bowl victory in 1986, has died, his family announced.
He was 86.

“It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka,” the family said in a statement Friday that did not include a cause of death.

“While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family,” the statement said. “Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.”
The Bears released a statement saying Ditka’s impact on the team as “a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable.”
Ditka, the statement said, “created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations.”

Ditka, who was inducted into the pro football Hall of Fame in 1988, was remembered by the organization’s president Jim Porter as a player who “brought an unrivaled level of toughness to an era already defined by physicality.”
“He brought that same philosophy to his coaching,” Porter said in a statement.

Tough and pugnacious, Ditka personified the hard-hitting team he led to a 46-10 thrashing of the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX and was called “Iron Mike,” both because of his gruff demeanor and because he hailed from a steel town in western Pennsylvania.
Ditka, who was born Michael Dyczko on Oct. 18, 1939, became a beloved figure in the Windy City and the embodiment of Chicago’s blue-collar, tough-guy identity.

In the years after the Bears won the Super Bowl, Ditka was immortalized by “Saturday Night Live” in the “Bill Swerski’s Superfans” sketches, which featured a group of fans singing his praises to the point of absurdity with tick Chicawgo ayccents.
“If I may shift gears for a moment gentlemen, coach Ditka vs. The Hurricane, who would win?” the Bill Swerski character says in one skit.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Ditka! Ditka!,” the others reply.
Ditka was married from 1961 to 1973 to his first wife, Marge. That marriage produced four children: Mark, Matt, Mike and Megan. In 1977, he married Diane Trantham, who also survives him.
The Ditka family has not yet announced any funeral arrangements.
The oldest of four children, Ditka was the son of a welder of Polish and Ukrainian stock who changed his name to make it easier to pronounce.

But growing up in the town of Aliquippa, Ditka excelled at the all-American sport of football and that earned him a scholarship and a ticket out of town to the University of Pittsburgh, where he initially planned to study dentistry.

Instead, Ditka excelled on the gridiron and in 1961 he was drafted by the Bears as a tight end. There, Ditka redefined a position that mostly consisted of blocking for rushers by becoming a scoring machine who racked up a dozen touchdowns in his first season and was named Rookie of the Year.

Ditka was a star on the 1963 Bears championship, in the pre-Super Bowl era, and a pro-bowler in each of the five seasons he played for “Da Bears.” He also gained some infamy by decking a fan who ran out on the field in the middle of a championship game broadcast on national TV.

“Ditka has been trained since high school to knock down anything that moves,” famous Chicago newspaper columnist Mike Royko wrote in Sept. 1966. “The young man flew into the air. He was limp when he landed and shaky when the police led him away.”
Unable to reach a contract agreement with Bears owner and coach George Halas, Ditka signed with the Houston Oilers in 1967 for the then-princely sum of $300,000.
Halas, Ditka said disparagingly, “threw nickels around like manhole covers.”
Ditka went on to play for the Dallas Cowboys, where in 1972 he caught a touchdown pass in their 24–3 victory over the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI.

After retiring in 1973, Ditka was hired by the Cowboys as an assistant coach. And during his nine seasons there, Dallas made the playoffs eight times, won six division titles, three NFC championships, and a Super Bowl victory in 1977.
“Ditka was the first man enshrined in Canton who had won Super Bowls as a player, assistant coach and head coach,” the Hall of Fame said in a statement.
In 1982, Ditka and Halas made peace and the former Bears tight end became the Bears head coach.
With his bushy mustache, combed back hair, and growly voice, Ditka actually looked a bit like the bear on the team’s logo, Chicago sports journalists noted.
“Give me three years, and if you walk with me, we’ll get to the dance,” Ditka reportedly vowed at a team meeting.

It took Ditka four years to get the team to the Super Bowl. And he did so with an old-school type of hard-nosed play that relied more on running than passing, a hard-hitting defense, and which he called “Bears Football.”

Powered by one of the most formidable defenses ever fielded by an NFL team and an offense led by unstoppable running back Walter Payton and gutsy quarterback Jim McMahon, the Bears quickly routed the Patriots in the championship game.
“There are teams that are fair-haired, and those that aren’t so fair-haired,” Ditka said at the time. “Some teams are named Smith, some Grabowski. We’re Grabowskis!”
They were swaggering Grabowskis.
The Bears were so confident they would win it all the team recorded a championship anthem called the “Super Bowl Shuffle” seven weeks before the Super Bowl.
Under Ditka, the Bears won several more divisional titles and played in seven playoff games. But Ditka never took the team back to the big dance.

Ditka suffered a heart attack during the 1988 season but the Bears mostly continued winning.  Five years later, after the Bears won just five games and lost 11 during the 1992 season, Halas fired Ditka.
He went on to become a football analyst on TV and then coached the New Orleans Saints for three losing seasons before he was fired from that job in 1999.
But Ditka never coached another NFL team again.
Instead, Ditka returned to the broadcast booth, working for NBC, CBS and ESPN and opened a chain of steakhouses.
Never one to shy away from the camera, Ditka co-starred in the 2005 comedy “Kicking & Screaming” alongside Will Ferrell and Robert Duvall, playing an over-the-top version of himself in the film.

Ditka also made numerous cameo appearances on various TV shows. And he embarked on a three-decade career as a ubiquitous TV pitchman for everything from Hanes underwear and erectile dysfunction medication to Campbell’s Chunky Soups.
In  2004, Ditka seriously considered running as a Republican for an open U.S. Senate seat in Illinois. He declined and that seat was won by future president Barack Obama.

Ditka, though, was highly critical of Obama’s presidency and considered himself an “ultra conservative.” But Ditka did visit the White House in 2011 with members of the Super Bowl-winning Bears team where he presented the president with a Bears jersey with the number 85 on it and “Obama” emblazoned on the back.
Traditionally, the Super Bowl-winning team visits the White House after the game, but in 1986 their scheduled visit was cancelled because of the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster.

“When I got to Chicago in the summer of 1985, Mike Ditka and the Chicago Bears were king,” Obama posted on X. “Coach Ditka set the tone for a team that was punishing, dominant, and fun — and the city loved him for it. I’m thinking of the Ditka family and Bears fans everywhere on the passing of a legend.”

But Ditka also rankled many fans in deep blue Chicago with his early and outspoken support for Donald Trump’s candidacy for president. And he sparked a backlash in 2017 when, during a radio interview, he criticized Black players for taking a knee during the singing of the National Anthem and said he wasn’t aware of any racial oppression in the U.S.
The very next day, Ditka apologized.
“I have absolutely seen oppression in society in the last 100 years,” Ditka said in statement to WGN-TV in Chicago. “The interview was about the NFL and related issues. That’s where my head was at.”
In 2024, after several years of living in Florida, Ditka moved back to Chicago.
“Chicago is my home,” he said.

title: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake rocks Panama
summary: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake shook the central coast of Panama on Friday, prompting tsunami warnings for several neighboring countries.
story: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake shook the central coast of Panama on Friday, prompting tsunami warnings for several neighboring countries.

The earthquake hit around 1:56 p.m. ET, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. Around three hours later, a second powerful earthquake measuring at 6.6 magnitude, struck Panama after a series of aftershocks, which registered magnitudes between 4.8 and 5.8, rippled across the southern tip of the country.
Seismologists at the University of Panama recorded more than 45 aftershocks, though many were too weak to be felt.
The U.S. Tsunami Center flagged tsunami warnings for Ecuador, Colombia, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Mexico, El Salvador, Costa Rica and Peru, as well as Panama, shortly after the quake.
The initial earthquake was centered about 6 miles southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, near Panama’s southern tip, the USGS said. It struck at a depth of 6 miles.
Tremors were also felt in the capital, Panama City, where buildings shook and people evacuated into the streets. The city is known for its tall skyscrapers.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news of the quake’s impact.

“We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but we’re OK, though we’re very scared,” Rosendo Domínguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, told The Associated Press by phone. “Everyone is outside, scared.”
Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service said the damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos.

Smith said several injuries have been reported, including one person struck by debris from a partially collapsed structure in the city of Penonomé. He confirmed a partial collapse and cracks at the cathedral in the district’s main square and the Dos Continentes hotel.

No fatalities were immediately reported, but Malitzie Rivera, deputy director of Panama Civil Protection said injured people “have been transferred to educational centers, health centers, and hospital centers.”

The province of Coclé said the governor’s palace there suffered significant structural damage, but that staff members were safely evacuated. The local government also urged community members to remain calm in the quake’s aftermath.
Video aired by local news outlets showed a Catholic cathedral collapsing and part of a hotel’s facade falling onto a car in the city of Penonomé, in the central province of Coclé.
Social media videos show collapsed buildings near the site of the original quake and the aftershocks, including a hotel reduced to rubble in the tourist-friendly Playa Venao.
Panama’s National System for Civil Protection said it is monitoring for further reports of damage throughout the country.
Panama lies along the “Ring of Fire,” the line of seismic faults encircling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world’s earthquakes occur.

Nearby countries sent messages of support Friday afternoon. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella, whose country was recently hit by earthquakes, expressed his solidarity with the Panamanian people and their government during what he called “difficult times.”
“Panama is not alone! You can count on Colombia’s support and our full willingness to provide whatever assistance is needed,” he wrote on X.
The U.S. Embassy in Panama said it was “closely monitoring” the aftermath of the quake and accounting for the welfare of its citizens in Panama, a well-known retirement destination for Americans.

title: Ben Affleck Admits He Trash Talks Kids Online While Playing ‘Fortnite’
summary: Ben Affleck recently revealed on the “New Heights” podcast that he sometimes gets into squabbles with kids on the internet while playing popular multiplayer open-world survival game “Fortnight.”
story: Gamer rage gets to everyone — even celebs.
Ben Affleck recently revealed on the “New Heights” podcast that he sometimes trash talks kids on the internet while playing popular multiplayer open-world survival game “Fortnight.”
Affleck, it appears, has a tough time taking the heat.

“Twelve-year-olds just f--- you up,” Affleck lamented to hosts Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on the Oct. 7 podcast episode. “I get killed right away and they taunt you and s--- like ‘You suck! F--- you!’”
Affleck acknowledged that he ends up “getting in arguments” with the kids in the game’s chat.
“F--- you! I don’t suck,” he says in response to the taunting, Affleck told the podcast hosts. “I’m a grown man.”

Affleck, who’s currently promoting crime-thriller film “Animals,” joined the podcast to discuss the project. He explained that the costumes in the film are inspired by some of the outfits, referred to as skins, in “Fortnite.” The video game famously features different skins that can be upgraded through milestones, challenges and more.
As Affleck points out in the podcast, the game has also dropped exclusive and limited edition skins that have become some of the most coveted aspects of the game.
“My son and he’s like ‘For Christmas, can you get me these real skins for Fortnite?’ But they’re 300 bucks,” Affleck tells the podcast of the virtual costumes.
Affleck has long been an avid gamer. On the podcast, he explained that in addition to first-person shooter games, he’s a fan of sports games like football game “Madden” and basketball game “NBA 2K.”

The actor has also been open about his love for “Valorant,” a first-person tactical hero shooter video game. He’s been spotted at major tournaments and even joined a watch party livestream last year with esports team Sentinels.

title: ‘Pretty Little Liars’ Actor Says He Was Held At Gunpoint and Knifepoint in Mugging Attack
summary: Actor Keegan Allen, best known for his role in teen drama series “Pretty Little Liars,” alleges in an Oct. 9 video that he was violently mugged in West Hollywood by two masked men.
story: Actor Keegan Allen, best known for his role in teen drama series “Pretty Little Liars,” alleges in an Oct. 9 video that he was violently mugged in West Hollywood by two masked men.

In the video that was posted to his Instagram account, Allen, who appears to be bleeding from his head, says that he was robbed outside of Laurel Supply, an upscale grocery store in the Los Angeles neighborhood.

“These two dudes hit me in the head and pointed a gun at me with a knife, and then took off,” a visibly bloody Allen, catching his breath, says in the graphic video. He adds that the attackers took his watch.
Responding to comments under his video, the 37-year-old told fans that he went to the hospital following the incident and was “def concussed.”

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department shared a statement in response to an NBC News request for comment on the incident. The department said that the LAPD’s Major Crimes Bureau is investigating the reported Oct. 8 armed robbery.
In the Instagram video, Allen shared footage of the alleged attack, which shows two men pointing a gun at a victim. One of the men bashes the victim over the head.
“Robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint by two young men that threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have! God said no tonight. My life for a watch,” he wrote in the caption of his post.
Allen wrote in response to a comment that one of the attackers also demanded a bracelet the actor was wearing, which led to the beating.
“I was trying to tell him it’s not easy to take off and said ‘you can take it off’ and he pistol whipped me,” Allen wrote.

The sheriff’s department said in the statement that deputies responded to the incident around 9:05 p.m. and spoke to a victim who reported being approached by two male suspects in black clothing. The victim told deputies that one suspect pointed a handgun at him while the other brandished a knife.
Actor Keegan Allen describes violent mugging incident

“During the incident, one of the suspects struck the victim in the face with the handgun, causing a laceration to his forehead,” the statement said. “The suspects took the victim’s watch and fled the location in an unknown vehicle.”
Personnel from the Los Angeles County Fire Department responded to the scene and medically evaluated the victim, who was not transported to the hospital, the statement said.
In his post, Allen called out Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass and California governor Gavin Newsom.
“Let’s hope all these flock cameras that @karenbassla @gavinnewsom and everyone thinks will stop crime can find these very dangerous criminals,” Allen wrote on Instagram.

In a statement sent to NBC News, Bass called the incident “egregious.” She also pointed out that West Hollywood is an independent city and that the LA County Sheriff’s Department is leading the investigation. It is technically not part of the city of Los Angeles.
“No one should have to experience something like this,” Bass said.

According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, serious crimes in the area have decreased nearly 10% from January through August. Additionally, robberies have been on the decline. Statistics show that through August, there were 49 reported robberies. That’s a 21% decrease from the 62 incidents during the same period in 2025.
In response to recent October incidents, a department spokesperson said that the agency is increasing the number of deputies conducting patrols throughout the city.
“While these declines are encouraging, they do not diminish the seriousness of recent robberies or the fear felt by our community,” a spokesperson for the department said.

title: There’s a New Britney Spears Song. Listen to ‘She’ll Never Be Me’
summary: Britney Spears fans got an unexpected surprise in the form of a previously unreleased song from the pop icon.
story: Britney Spears fans got an unexpected surprise in the form of a previously unreleased song from the pop icon.
On Oct. 9, Spears and her team dropped the song “She’ll Never Be Me,” which was recorded for her 2001 self-titled third album “Britney.”
The song comes weeks before the album celebrates its 25th anniversary with a special edition re-release, “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition),” that includes songs from the vault.
“She’ll Never Be Me” is a quintessential Britney Spears track with its bubblegum pop, early aughts sound, girl power lyrics and the singer’s signature girlish and gritty vocals.
The 3-minute track talks about a former lover who is now with someone that looks just like her.

“You know I’m one of a kind/Boy, what’s this I see/Your girl, she looks just like me/Blond hair and dressed to a T,” she begins. “You tell me how can this be/Does she know I was the one/Who used to turn you on/But you don’t want to talk about it.”
According to the song’s YouTube description, Spears is credited as the lyricist, associated performer and composer.
Her ex Justin Timberlake is also featured as a lyricist and composer, along with Bradley Daymond and Alex Greggs. Riprock ‘n’ Alex G is a producer.

“She’ll Never Be Me” is one of five new songs included in the “Britney” re-release, including “Am I a Sinner,” “When I Say So,” “My Big Secret” and “Right Now (Taste The Victory)” from her 2002 Pepsi commercial.
Fans will get to hear the songs when “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition)” is released on Nov. 6.
The last time Spears shared a new song was 2023’s “Mind Your Business” with Will.i.am. In 2020, she also dropped a never-before-heard collaboration with the Backstreet Boys titled “Matches.”
The song was featured in a deluxe edition of her 2016 album “Glory.”

title: Crystal Harris Posts Message She Sent Jessica Biel With Plea to ‘Reconsider’ Playing Hugh Hefner’s Wife in Movie
summary: Hugh Hefner’s widow, Crystal Harris, is asking Jessica Biel not to portray a fictional version of the Playboy founder’s wife in the upcoming movie “Playmates.”
story: Hugh Hefner’s widow, Crystal Harris, is asking Jessica Biel not to portray a fictional version of the Playboy founder’s wife in the upcoming movie “Playmates.”

Harris, who was married to Hefner from 2012 until his death in 2017, posted a screenshot of a text on Instagram on Oct. 8 that she sent Biel, urging her to pass up the role of Hefner’s fictional wife.
“Please reconsider playing Hugh Hefner’s ‘wife’ if this film intends to romanticize him or the Playboy world,” Harris wrote in a message to Biel, according to the screenshot she shared on Instagram.

“I was actually his wife, and I experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse in that relationship. Many other women have come forward with allegations of rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation as well.

“There are also deeply troubling concerns involving minors. I hope everyone involved in this film takes the time to listen to the women who lived it before helping Hollywood turn it back into nostalgia.”
TODAY.com has reached out to Biel for comment about Harris’ post, as well as Harris for any further comment about what she wrote. Neither responded.
TODAY.com also reached out toHefner’s estate for comment about Harris’ allegations of experiencing “rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation,” but did not hear back.
The film is being made by Searchlight Pictures, which not did reply to TODAY.com’s request for comment about Harris’ post or Biel’s casting in the movie.

Variety reported Oct. 6 that Biel has joined the cast of “Playmates,” a coming-of-age story about a 13-year-old girl who befriends a woman competing with other hopefuls to become Playmate of the Month. Bill Pullman, Lily-Rose Depp and Indiana Elle are also attached to star in it.
Biel is slated to play Hefner’s wife in the movie. According to Variety, the character is fictional and not based on a real person.
Hefner was married two other times, to Kimberley Conrad from 1989 to 2010 and Millie Williams from 1949 to 1959.
Harris followed up her post with another one, in which she showed appreciation for the “overwhelming response” she received.
“So many women are speaking up, sharing their experiences, and expressing that they’ve simply had enough,” she wrote.

“Victim blaming is still far too common, especially when it comes to narcissistic and emotional abuse. I know that not everyone has experienced these dynamics firsthand, and I’m genuinely glad for those who haven’t. But I also hope we can listen to and support the women who have, even when their experiences are difficult to understand.”

Harris also said she wants “to support women” and express her hope that the movie is “not something that will glorify Hugh Hefner. With women in the leading roles, my hope is that the film ultimately delivers a message of empowerment: that women can find fulfillment, independence, and a sense of self beyond Playboy.”
In 2024, Harris penned a memoir, “Only Say Good Things: Surviving ‘Playboy’ and Finding Myself,” in which she wrote that living in the famed Playboy Mansion was like living in a prison.

“I always had to be home by six o’clock. If I wasn’t, it was a problem. He would be upset. He would be yelling my name through the house,” she says of Hugh Hefner, writing that she felt like Rapunzel locked in a tower.
“I didn’t know then that I could rescue myself. I didn’t always know I needed to be rescued, but I knew I was trapped,” she added.
Harris also said Hefner was a “narcissist” and had a need to control the women who lived in the mansion.
“It’s like he wanted us to beg him for something, so he could feel even more powerful and probably have us feel small,” she told TODAY.com in 2024.
“It was weird and it was hard. Looking back, he did use me and manipulate me for his own gain in every way,” she continued.
In August, Harris said Hefner was “very abusive” and that she was “brainwashed” when she appeared on the “No One Asked Her” podcast.

“So I just thought I was the crazy one because all of the media put Hef on such a pedestal that I’m like, ‘OK, if they all see him as this larger-than-life amazing human, there must be something wrong with me,” she said.
Hefner has been accused of sexual misconduct before, with multiple allegations leveled against him in the 2022 A&E series “Secrets of Playboy,” released five years after he died in 2017.

“This series contains allegations of wrongdoing over decades by Hugh Hefner and others associated with him,” read a statement at the end of each episode. “The vast majority of allegations have not been the subject of criminal investigations or charges, and they do not constitute proof of guilt.”

title: How Realistic Is ‘War’? A Divorce Lawyer Says this 1 Move Would Get Characters Disbarred
summary: A UK divorce lawyer reacts to the HBO drama “War” including the mole and serving papers on the red carpet.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this story, a U.K. divorce lawyer weighs in on “War.”

HBO’s new legal drama “War” gives viewers an unflinching look behind the scenes of a nasty, high-powered divorce. The series focuses on the lengths divorce lawyers from rival law firms in London will go to score a profitable win for their clients.

The depiction of ruthless attorneys scheming to gain the upper hand in a pending divorce “heavily dramatized for viewing public consumption,” and not necessarily realistic, said Daniel Sugaré, the head of family law department at Sugaré & Co. Solicitors in the U.K.

Set in London, “War” tells the story of the shattering end of the decade-long marriage between tech billionaire Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) and his Hollywood star wife, Carla Duval (Sienna Miller), resulting in divorce.
Morgan and Carla hire lawyers from rival London law firms, Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne, respectively, to take each other down in court.
Here’s what a real divorce lawyer thinks of the show’s pilot.
Hiring a Lawyer As a Mole? That’s a Big No-No
One of lawyers’ most egregious antics would cause them to lose their law licenses in real life, Sugaré said.
Specifically, Cathcarts & Sons’s move to send struggling young lawyer Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) to Taylor & Byrne to act as a mole for their case.
“(Johnny) would be struck off immediately by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA),” Sugaré said of the mole.
“You’ve got a duty to your clients to act confidentially, act in their best interests, and by sharing information like in that manner, that they would be bound for disciplinary procedures,” he added.
The higher-ups at Cathcarts & Sons who orchestrated the scheme “would also face significant legal consequences from the SRA and potentially criminal proceedings,” he said.
The bad behavior of the lawyers on the show veers far from what real-life attorneys aim to do: help clients remain calm and focused so they can come to an agreement.
“In certain cases, you have to act in an aggressive way to protect your client’s interest,” said Sugaré. “But in the show, it seems like they’re doing that more than what is necessary.”
Carla’s Cheating Scheme

The show starts with Morgan sleeping with a young woman named Flora (Rose Williams). Turns out the moment has been orchestrated by Carla. She wants to prove that Morgan is unfaithful, and in doing so, exploit the prenuptial’s infidelity clause.
But will Carla’s scheme actually work? Not so fast, Sugaré said.
“An affair is not ordinarily a legal escape route from a prenuptial agreement,” Sugaré said.
Sugaré said infidelity clauses are “unusual” in England, as prenups generally deal with financial agreements rather than penalties for cheating.

“Even if this agreement contains an infidelity clause, Carla could not assume that the court would enforce it. While these cases are fact specific, proof of an affair would not ordinarily invalidate the agreement or entitle her to a larger settlement,” he said.
Serving Papers on the Red Carpet
Morgan and Carla race to be the one to serve the other with divorce papers. Morgan ultimately Carla divorce papers on a red carpet.
It’s a biting and humiliating moment, but not necessarily a tactic that gives Morgan an edge, according to Sugaré.
“The race to start divorce proceedings makes good television, but being the applicant does not give Morgan priority over the assets or make the judge more sympathetic to him,” Sugaré said.
And while serving a divorce application on a red carpet is “legally permissible,” it’s normally facilitated via email, Sugaré says.
So, Is Divorce Really ‘War’?
As for the show’s title? Sugaré said war is an apt metaphor for the potential brutality of divorce.
“It can get aggressive. It can be vicious. It can be personal, and the job of the lawyer is to try and rein your client in,” Sugaré said.

He explained a good lawyer tries to help clients stop ruminating about their emotions and the end of the marriage and instead prepare to “reach sensible agreements or make big decisions about (their) future,” he said.
His advice for anyone entering into a marriage? At the risk of sounding like an “anti-love guy,” Sugaré suggests both parties sign a prenuptial agreement.

“In the right circumstances, a prenuptial agreement can give both parties clarity and certainty. It may not be the most romantic conversation before a wedding, but being open about finances at the outset can prevent far greater conflict later.”

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Michael Douglas’ Explosive Memoir
summary: Actor Michael Douglas, who cemented his legendary status after a decadeslong career in Hollywood,” reflects on his wildly eventful life in new memoir “One Helluva Ride.”
story: Actor Michael Douglas, who cemented his legendary status after a decadeslong career in Hollywood,” reflects on his wildly eventful life in new memoir “One Helluva Ride.” And that includes some pretty explosive confessions.

Douglas, best known for his roles in blockbuster films “Wall Street” and “Basic Instinct,” details his personal sagas involving everything from infidelity to struggles with parenting in what many readers have already considered a bombshell of a book.
